articles.body:
Rings of Power is a Prime Video original based on J.R.R. Tolkien's history of Middle-earth. The series takes place well before the events of The Lord of the Rings, focusing on the major events of the world's Second Age. Since the story isn't directly adapting a specific book , it does take some liberties with the direction the dramatization takes. You can consider this series to be outside of The Lord of the Rings movie lor e you already know.

The Rings of Power is a Prime Video original, which means you can only watch it with an Amazon Prime subscription. There are multiple free trials available to new subscribers if you don't already have access. With Amazon's Black Friday sale happening this month, 30 days free can go a long way.

In addition to being able to watch the series on Prime Video, you can now also own 4K and Blu-ray editions of the first two seasons. The limited edition steelbooks aren't out until December 1 , but you can get the standard copies ahead of season 3.

The Rings of Power Season 1 [Limited Edition 4K Steelbook]

The Rings of Power Season 2 [Limited Edition 4K Steelbook]

There have been two full seasons of Rings of Power so far with season 3 releasing throughout November. It was reported earlier this year that the series is still on track for five seasons , as per Amazon's initial deal for rights.

IGN reviewed all eight episodes of The Rings of Power season 1 and gave the series an 8 out of 10. Here's a quick summary of what we thought:

"The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power largely succeeds by staying faithful to J. R. R. Tolkien’s themes and tone, if not all the specifics of his canon. Some inconsistent plotting and unnecessary misdirection slows it down, but doesn’t derail the story, and when it reaches its climax in the sixth episode it all comes together brilliantly. Amazon’s massive budget has produced some of the most remarkable sets and scenes ever on TV, creating a strong successor to Peter Jackson’s beloved Lord of the Rings trilogy. Yet The Rings of Power also remembers it’s the little moments of humor and character growth that really make Middle-earth really come alive." - Samantha Nelson

The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power - Exclusive Images

IGN reviewed all eight episodes of The Rings of Power season 2 and gave the series a 6 out of 10. Here's a quick summary of what we thought:

"Season 2 of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power does a great job portraying Sauron’s machinations and his impact on those he manipulates, but too much time is spent on disconnected subplots delivering only mediocre intrigue and thin characters. A tighter season would have been great, but the moments of powerful pathos and dramatic action the season does deliver are bogged down by scenes focused on places and people who will only become important later in the saga of Middle-earth." - Samantha Nelson

articles.title: Forest Temple - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Forest Temple Dungeon Walkthrough section covers both the Nintendo 64 and Nintendo 3DS versions of Zelda OOT,
articles.body:
This The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Forest Temple Dungeon Walkthrough section covers both the Nintendo 64 and Nintendo 3DS versions of Zelda OOT, including the Nintendo Switch Online/eShop version from 2026. We will cover each and every secret, puzzle, boss fight, and item in this guide to the Forest Temple, the fourth dungeon.

Ocarina of Time: Forest Temple Walkthrough

When you first enter the dungeon you'll be ambushed by two Wolfos. Wait until they attack, dodge, and then stab them in the back to kill them instantly.

Go up the vines to the right (if you're facing the door) and Hookshot to the chest on the other side of the room to get your very first Small Key .

Gold Skulltula : There's a Gold Skulltula up high on the vines. Use your hookshot to kill it and also retrieve the Golden Skull Token it drops.

Enter the door, kill the Skulltula in the hallway with the Hookshot (you can shoot it on either side with the Hookshot to kill it) and enter the main room of the dungeon. Four Poes steal the light from the torches in the room.

This makes the elevator inactive; you must defeat the four Poes hidden in the Temple to light all of the torches, and regain use of the elevator.

Go to the room straight ahead, where there's a Gold Skulltula on the wall to the right of the door.

Go through the door, kill the Blue Bubble (as long as it is surrounded by flames, it cannot be harmed. Touch it with your shield or use the Hookshot to ground it and then slash away with the sword to dispatch it.) In the next room a pair of Stalfos is your opponent.

Keep your shield up at all times, as they are powerful foes. The Stalfos take very broad swings, opening up part of their body for damage. Slash at them as soon as you see them get ready to attack. The prize for victory is a Small Key .

Head back into the main room, heading to the blue block in the corner to your right, and play the Song of Time. Go through the door into the next room and climb the vines on the right all the way to the top, making sure to free the path of the Skulltulas with your Hookshot beforehand. To reach the very last one, stand right next to the wall and look straight up at it. Go through the door and slay the lone Blue Bubble to make a treasure chest with the Dungeon Map appear. Enter the next room.

You arrive on a balcony on the other side of the door. Fire your Hookshot at the target just above the balcony to the left. Step on the red switch to drain the water from the nearby well. Jump off the balcony to the ground below.

Gold Skulltula : In this room on the west side of the map, there is a small chest (containing a measly Recovery Heart) on the elevated platform. Target it with you Hookshot to reach the Gold Skulltula on the wall.

There is room on the east side of the temple that looks just like this one. It, too, contains a Gold Skultulla, sitting on a small "island" in the water. Retrieve it when you pass through.

Climb the ladder down into the well and follow the short tunnel to a chest containing a Small Key . Climb the vines and return once again to the main room. Unlock the locked door up the stairs to your right (It's the only locked door in the room). Defeat the Skulltula and enter the next room.

After eliminating the Blue Bubble, climb the ladders to the second floor. Following the direction of the arrows painted on the ground, move the blue block as close as you can to the large square indentation on the ground (first by pulling it, then by pushing it). When you can't push it anymore, circle around by heading through the tunnel where the box was and take a right to locate the block. Continue to push the block until it fits into the indentation.

Find the ladder in the hallway where you originally found the blue box and climb up. Push the red block until it hits the wall. Return to the blue block and use it to hoist yourself up to the next level, where you can continue pushing the red box down the hall until it locks into place. Use it to climb up and take a right at the end of the hall. Climb the ladder and defeat the two Blue Bubble. Unlock the door (ignore the eye for now) and walk down the twisted corridor.

In the next room, watch out for Wall Masters, shadowed hands that can grab you and take you back to the entrance of the temple. They appear only if you linger in one spot for too long. Quickly jump over the platforms and unlock the door. Walk down the stairs and enter the door.

This next room pits you against a lone Stalfos, who only gets replaced by two more Stalfos upon his death. Be careful not to fall down into the room below. Dispatch these guys the same way as you did previously; the only difference is that if you don’t kill the third Stalfos fast enough, the second Stalfos will piece itself back together. If you are having trouble killing them fast enough, try changing targets after each successful blow. If you do this, once the second Stalfos is dead, the last Stalfos will only take one hit to kill. You will earn the Fairy Bow from this fight.

Exit to the opposite side of where you entered and find the three paintings along the steps. Two of the paintings are black and the other has a picture of a Blue Poe in it. The Poe is very shy and will quickly migrate to another painting if you get too close. Shoot each picture with the Poe in it until the Poe is released from the last picture.

Go downstairs and fight the first Poe sister. Lock onto her and shoot her with your bow (or slash her with your sword) only when she is visible. Block or avoid her spinning attack and patiently wait for her body to appear to cause damage to her. You can use a Deku Seed to make her reappear immediately. With her death, one of the flames is returned to the central chamber and a treasure chest containing the Compass appears.

Go back to the room where you fought the Stalfos and enter the door on the opposite side, where you will find another three paintings, this time housing a Red Poe. Repeat the strategy you used against the Blue Poe Sister.

Get the Small Key from the treasure chest that appears. Go back upstairs, jump across the platforms, and cross the twisted hallway. In the room with the two Blue Bubbles, correct the alignment of the hallway by shooting the eye above the door with your recently acquired bow.

Cross the now level hallway and enter the room to see the gold and blue colored treasure chest on the ground below, which contains the Boss Key .

Retrieve the key, then jump down the nearby hole and eliminate the enemies to unlock the door. You'll wind up on a ledge above a room you've visited previously. Be careful not to fall. Head through the dungeon door in the aclove by the wooden door and kill the Floormaster.

Once defeated, the Floormaster will split into three tiny Floormasters. Be careful, if a mini-floormaster grabs onto you, it will drain a signifcant amount of your life and regrow into a full sized Floormaster. Once the room is free of enemies, open the treasure chest that appears to get a Small Key .

Exit and go through the door on your right to return to a familiar-looking room. Climb up to the entrance to the twisted hallway. Hit the eye once more to contort the hallway again, and head through it. Return to where you fought the Blue Poe and continue through the locked door.

Leap towards the opening to the hallway on the right to encounter a stationary variation of the Bubble monsters, which can be quickly eliminated with arrows. Go through the locked door, jump across the spinning platforms, and use Din’s Fire on the frozen eye. If you don’t have Din’s Fire, circle around the platform, line your arrow up with the flame and the frozen eye, and shoot an arrow to melt the ice. Either way, the eye will close and the hallway will become twisted. Run through the hallway and jump down the hole in the northeast corner of the room.

You’ll land in a room with a tiled floor. The ceiling above falls down periodically, so you won’t be able to cross over to the other side in one move. Look at the ceiling and note the holes in it. Let the ceiling drop once and then immediately run to the tile with the switch on it, carefully avoiding the Skulltulas that drop down from the ceiling (you may want to take them out with arrows ahead of time). Then run to the tile to the left of the chest, which contains arrows. Let the ceiling drop one more time, and then run to the door.

Shoot the painting with the green Poe in it. Blocks will fall from the ceiling and you’ll have one minute to push them all together. One of the blocks (colored blue) is extra so push or pull it off to the side. Use the big painting as reference. The blocks are all already in the right corners so just bring them all together evenly.

After you piece the blocks together, the Green Poe appears. Defeat it the same way you defeated the others and go through the door. Shoot down the Skulltula on the ceiling and go through the door. Jump off the balcony to battle the final Poe Sister.

This Poe fights differently from her kin. She clones herself and surrounds you, in an attempt to prevent you from attacking the real Poe. The dead giveaway, though, is that the real Poe does a twirl each time she appears. L-target this Poe and fire an arrow at her. Repeat this process five times to kill her. With all the flames returned to their proper place, the elevator in the center of the room returns. Use it to enter the room below.

Before you can fight the boss, you have to go through one more puzzle. The room is divided up in a series of pillars, cages, and switches. Push a pillar counter-clockwise one to reveal a switch. Press the switch, then rotate the room counter-clockwise again, to reveal another switch. Press it and rotate the room in the same direction as before, to open up a room with a Skulltula, a chest containing some arrows, and a Gold Skulltula climbing on the wall.

Push the pillar counter-clockwise one more time to gain access to the final switch. Press it to open the gate on the opposite side of the room, leading to the Boss's Chamber. Go through the large locked door.

Walk up the stairs and move to the center of the room. Make an attempt to walk back to the stairs; the gate will close in front of you. Link turns around to a very big surprise: Phantom Ganon .

Phantom Ganon gallops off into one of the paintings. Stand in the very center of the room with your bow and arrow drawn and keep panning the room to see which painting Ganon will pop out of. Two Phantom Ganons run down from two different paintings; one is real, the other is not. The fake one turns around (and is a bit lighter colored than the real one), while the real one starts to emerge from the painting. Unleash an arrow into the real one before he can leave the painting. If you can't hit him in time, rush to the sides to avoid his attack.

After the third hit, Phantom Ganon abandons this tactic and dismounts from his horse. Phantom Ganon will then float around the room and shoot a single projectile, which you must slash at to deflect it back at him. The taste of his own medicine brings him down to the ground, where you can proceed to stab and slash him as many times as you can before he returns to the air. As the fight wears on, Phantom Ganon becomes aware of your strategy, deflecting back your deflected shots in a furious ping-pong match until one of you loses. Eventually, Phantom Ganon crumbles before your might and leaves behind a Heart Container . Enter the blue portal.

For a more in-depth description for defeating this boss, see Phantom Ganon for more information.

Saria gives you the Forest Medallion . You are transported back to where the Great Deku Tree stands. In front of it springs the cheerful Deku Tree Sprout.

Gold Skulltula : Visit Kokiri Village at night. Between the two trunks of the twins house is a lone Gold Skulltula. Kill it and get the Golden Skull Token with the Hookshot.

If you're in real need of some rupees, go to the Lost Woods and immediately head left, to where your Skull Kid friend resides. He doesn't like you too much now that you're an adult. Don't do any fancy attacks, stick with horizontal swipes and stabs. After several hits the Skull Kid will go down and surrenders a Huge Rupee , worth 200 rupees. Exit the room and come back for as much money as you need.

Go see Sheik at the Temple of Time to learn the Prelude of Light, a song that warps you back to the Temple of Time. Plus, you can now travel back and forth in time by returning the Master Sword to its pedestal.

Now that you have the Fairy Bow, you can use Epona to collect Bottle #4 (see Bottle Locations ).

Your next destination is Kakariko Village .

articles.body:
Iron Maiden is a Skellige Side Quest with a suggested level of 19. Out of all the potential love interests in The Witcher 3, the character that Iron Maiden centers around is certainly one of the more interesting and eclectic options; she's worth learning more about.

You can pick this quest up from Jutta. She is directly east of Harviken. After talking to Jutta, she wants Geralt to find a sword from a sunken ship, and then she will challenge him to a fight.

Head west from Harviken towards the map marker. Once you are close, you will encounter multiple Ekhindnas. Once you have dealt with them, dive into the water, use your Witcher Senses to find and loot the sword.

Once you have the sword, head back to Jutta and give her the sword. After giving the sword to her, you can then challenge her to a sword fight.

After defeating her, she will invite Geralt to her home after dusk. Head towards her home and meditate until dusk, then talk to her. There is a romance option available here, or you can tell her to try searching the other isles for a man who can beat her in a sword fight.

The reward for completing Iron Maiden is 25 x experience.

articles.title: Spiritual Stone of Water - Zora Domain and Lake Hylia Walkthrough - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains
articles.body:
Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains the same, there's plenty of new differences to be found while exploring Hyrule. With the Spiritual Stone of Fire gained from clearing Dodongo's Cavern of its fearsome beast, Link will only have one left to obtain: the Spiritual Stone of Water, held by the Zoras who live at the source of the river that feeds Hyrule. However, you'll soon find they have their own problems to deal with involving a missing princess and a giant deity fish.

By now, you should have followed through on Darunia's advice to visit the Great Fairy atop Death Mountain (and her hint to visit her fellow Great Fairy sister hiding near Hyrule Castle. Armed with a new magic meter, Din's Fire, and an improved Spin Attack, Impa will have given you a new heading to find the next Spiritual Stone: by following the stream feeding Hyrule Field up to its source, located just southeast of the entrance to Kakariko Village.

Heading through a large tunnel, you'll arrive at a winding ravine and home of the mighty Zora River, and its powerful currents mean you won't be swimming upstream.

Instead, take a moment to speak with Kaepora Gaebora the Owl to learn more about the land. Much like the Gorons, the Zora don't get outside visitors often, save for the messengers of the Royal Family, so be prepared to demonstrate your credentials.

With your newly-acquired Bomb Bag, blow up the cracked boulders blocking your path, and note the odd plant in the ground surrounded by butterflies before moving up to introduce yourself to a strange man munching on snacks by a sealed gate.

This Bean Seller has a lot of Magic Beans to sell, but with a little twist. As of now, they won't be all that popular, but as you purchase them, demand will unexpectedly increase, driving up the price by 10 Rupees each time (It's you, you're the demand).

The effect of the Magic Beans won't be fully appreciated now, as you'll have to wait several years for the beans to grow into something useful, but trust me, they make a good investment. All of the patches of soft soil you've seen (and hopefully been putting Bugs in to find Gold Skulltulas) are all viable for a Magic Bean to be planted, so start with the one nearest to you (but not before dropping a bug in to find a new Gold Skulltula).

If you have the funds, we recommend buying at least 2 Magic Beans for now, and then a few more after finishing your tasks around the Zora's Domain if you want to conserve some money. After you plant it, jump across the raging river using the ledge to get around the sealed gate.

As you do, be prepared for annoying enemies called Octoroks to harass you from the water. They tend to lurk below the waters until they are ready to strike, jumping up and launching projectiles at you. Since they stay floating for a moment, you can simply halt and shield up, and bounce their attack right back at them to shut them up.

As you jump back across to the left side of the river, note that there's a lone Cucco over by the other side of the sealed gate the Bean Seller was sitting by. Remember that spot, and then continue upriver along the left side.

As you do, look for a large alcove along the northern cliff walls to find a small frog watching you from a series of stumps. He seems to be in a musical mood, so step and play a song for him and his friends -- any song!

With each unique song you play, one of the frogs will swell in size, and they'll reward you in increments of +5 Rupees, which means a total of 50 Rupees for the following songs:

Be sure to return as you learn more songs, and the rewards will be even greater!

Continue up the path, and deal with the new variant of Blue Tektites that can skim and jump across the water. Their only advantage is lost when you lure them to dry ground, where you can deflect their attack and jump strike to finish them off.

As you climb up to find a path leading further east, be sure to look back where the river splits down to the southwest. There's a trail of Rupees should you fall in, but there's also a high ledge at the back of the large island in the middle of the river. You can't swim up to it... but you can float to it.

Return back to the sealed gate by the start of the river and grab the lone Cucco. With all the enemies nearby defeated, you can safely escort it, throwing it over the last ledge before you climb up, and then use it to float down to the high platform, and use the vines to climb up to the top of the island.

At the top, you'll find a crumbling ruin with a large cracked boulder you can bomb to reveal a Grotto, which leads down to a Fairy Fountain -- good for restocking if you had to use any on Death Mountain.

Looking north, you can spot a high platform over the singing frogs that holds a Piece of Heart, but no way to reach it. Instead, head to the southern part of the island and across to a high ledge that hides a second Grotto entrance. In here, you'll find a Treasure Chest with a Business Scrub Seed ... as well as another Cucco!

Grab the Cucco and take him with you as you exit the Grotto, and then cross to the narrow platform where a Sheikah Stone is. From here, leap down to the Heart Piece using the second Cucco to float across!

Be sure to take that same Cucco with you as you continue up the Zora River trail, rather than leaving him inaccessible on some high platform. There will be a few more Ocotoks to dodge, but the area around the falls hiding the entrance to Zora's Domain is clear.

There are several crossing platforms here, and one leads up to a deep pool of water you can't swim down yet. On the other side, a high ledge overlooks a second Piece of Heart on a tiny platform to the northwest. Use that Cucco you held earlier to do one more floating jump across the falls to reach it.

While inspecting the area around the falls, be careful you don't fall in, or you might get swept back the way you came. If you jump down at the base of the falls, the water here is pretty shallow, and there's vines near a central platform to take you back up. Be sure to stick around this area at night, as a Gold Skulltula will appear around the backside of where the vines are for you to defeat.

At the top of the arching platforms is a spot for you to stand before the mighty falls. A plaque in front of them simply reads "Sleepless Waterfall - The flow of this waterfall serves the royal family of Hyrule. When the princess slumbers, so too do these falls". Good thing we know of a song to put these falls to sleep. Play "Zelda's Lullaby", and the waterfall will part, revealing the secret home of the Zora people.

The serene looking grotto known as Zora's Domain is comprised of two pools of water, with a large staircase and falls linking the two, and thankfully there's ample walkways for those who don't prefer swimming.

You can speak to the group of Zoras along the pool at the bottom. Some of them are practicing diving from the instructor at the top of the falls, while another seem to be frantically searching for a wayward princess.

Make your way up the grand staircase to find King Zora, a very large fellow that presides over a large chamber that you can walk up to address him from the dais over the water below. Speaking to the King, it seems both of your problems are linked - the now missing Princess Ruto carries the Spiritual Stone of Water with her, but nobody in all of the domain seems to be able to locate her. While initially ready to accept your aid, the King will realize your inability to swim limits how much you can help, and advises you to wait.

There's nothing wrong with getting a little training though, so look for the waterway leaving the audience chamber and over to the top of a large waterfall where a Diving Instructor is. He'll challenge you to improve your skills by seeking out five scales that he will toss into the waters below, and give you 40 seconds to find them all.

Leap down into the water, and hold A to dive into the water when swimming above the shimmering blue scales. Given that the controls are a lot more easier to handle than they were on the Nintendo 64, you should be able to locate and nab all five scales with plenty of time to spare.

As a reward, the Diving Instructor will bestow upon you a Silver Scale, allowing you to dive to much deeper depths than you could initially.

Note that this also allows you to use the pool of water outside the entrance to Zora's Domain to find a shortcut to the Lost Woods!

Before heading back down to test your new diving skills, note the two lit torches at the entrance to the audience chamber. You can use a Deku Stick and run down the steps to light torches along the way.

Keep running between torches and then stowing your stick before taking it out again as you head down to the bottom level, and follow a path behind the large waterfall to find two final braziers to light, which will reveal a Treasure Chest in the middle holding a Piece of Heart.

One of the Zora in the water has mentioned his diving accidentally taking him out of domain entirely, and if you look closely, you can spot a small hole in the wall in the main pool, and with your Silver Scale, you can now dive down deep enough to swim through and be transported all the way to the other side of Hyrule!

If you haven't been to Lake Hylia yet, you're in for a treat. Located on the south side of Hyrule, the massive lake is home to several points of interest, a large underwater ruin, and a few Zora out looking for the princess.

Notice a stream of bubbles coming from straight ahead of you as you swim out into the lake, they appear to be coming from an object underwater. Thanks to your new Silver Scale, you have enough power to touch the bottom of this shallower area and grab the object, swimming up to reveal an Empty... or not-so-empty Bottle!

Head to shore and use the bottle to read the contents: It's from Princess Ruto herself, who is trapped in the belly of the Zora's deity fish, Lord Jabu-Jabu! Despite her plea, it's probably best you bring this new back to King Zora.

First however, there's a few things you'll want to do around Lake Hylia.

Start by checking out the large observatory building nearby. The old man inside is researching the waters of Lake Hylia, and will invite you to test your diving skills in the nearby pool... but you still can't get to the bottom.

Outside, you can find a patch of soft soil, so be sure to plant one of your Magic Beans, and also send a Bug from a bottle in to scare up a Gold Skulltula.

On the eastern side of the shoreline, you can find two dancing scarecrows. One of them, Pierre, wants to wander the land in search of soul-shaking tunes. Give him a tune and he'll play it back for you, and suggest you play something for his friend who has a great memory.

When talking to Bonooru, he'll ask that you play a full custom song on your Ocarina. It can be anything you want, as long as it's a full eight notes long. Once you do, he'll boast that he has it memorized. Surely, this will be important later, so write that song down somewhere...

Heading along the rope bridge past the observatory, you can find Kaepora Gaebora next to an old gravestone, who will offer you a lift back to Hyrule Castle should you need it. Pull back the headstone, and you'll find a small tomb with four torches (use Din's Fire on three of them) and you'll summon a Treasure Chest with a Red Rupee.

The main island has a large tree, a pedestal that seems similar to others you've encountered, and a plaque that's too covered in dirt to read, so there's not much to do here yet.

Instead, start swimming for the far shores to the southwest. There's a couple more things to find here, including a pot with a Fairy.

Along the southern tip, look for the smallest of ledges you can climb up to find a tunnel entrance. You can shuffle through to the other side, where you'll find a Gold Skulltula.

Finally, across the water from the two scarecrows is Lake Hylia's own Fishing Pond. It's here you can rent out a fishing rod and try your luck and landing a big haul! The set-up is pretty straightforward: try to find a big-looking fish in the middle of the pod, cast your line near it, then gently pull back with ZR and wiggle your line to get its attention.

When it does, you'll need to alternate holding left or right -- whichever direction the fish is trying to flee in, until it gets tired and stops for a moment. When it does, hold down ZR and keep reeling in until it resumes its frantic escape. Keep it up, and the fish will be yours.

The owner is pretty good at judging the size at a distance, and if you bring him anything over 40cm, and you'll be awarded a Piece of Heart!

Now it's time to return to Zora's Domain with news of Princess Ruto's whereabouts. Head back to King Zora and open the bottle when standing before him, so that he can read the note himself.

While he doesn't want the rest of the people knowing that their deity may have accidentally swallowed the Princess, you'll be the perfect person to go on a rescue mission! But Lord Jabu-Jabu won't open his mouth for just anyone.

After King Zora finishes his grand and dramatic act of moving aside to open the path to Lord Jabu-Jabu, head back down to the bottom of the domain. In the corner of the shallows that connect to the path up to the shop, you can find a Zora trying desperately to catch an offering for Lord Jabu-Jabu. With the Empty Bottle you now have from giving away Ruto's Letter, use the bottle to catch one of the fish in the shallows, and head outside.

You'll now be face to face with the giant Lord Jabu-Jabu, who doesn't seem to be doing so hot. Before you give your offering however, it's worth exploring his grounds.

Off to the south, you can find a shallow path leading to a section of land with a few trees and a large cracked wall. Be sure to try rolling into the narrow tall trees here, and you can dislodge a Gold Skulltula!

Finally, bomb open the large cracked wall, and you'll reveal the entrance to a new Great Fairy Fountain. As with the others, you'll need to make an bigger offering again, this one totaling 100 Rupees this time.

Do so, and you'll meet the Great Fairy of Magic, who will offer you a new power: Farore's Wind. This with magic, you can essentially set a point anywhere within a dungeon, to travel back to in a flash by using the magic power again. This will work even if you leave the dungeon, should you need to resupply or take a break!

With this new upgrade in hand, leave the Great Fairy Fountain and approach Lord Jabu-Jabu. Look for a small offering receptacle, and take out a fish that you've bottled. Sensing a tasty snack, Lord Jabu-Jabu will open wide, sucking up everything around -- including you! Your next dungeon adventure will be a bit of an unorthodox one: It's inside Lord Jabu-Jabu himself !

Up Next: Lord Jabu-Jabu's Belly Dungeon Walkthrough

articles.body:
Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains the same, there's plenty of new differences to be found while exploring Hyrule. With the Zora Princess Ruto missing, Link has been tasked to find her within the depths of Lord Jabu-Jabu's Belly itself, and locate the Spiritual Stone of Water she was carrying.

With an offering of a tasty fresh fish, Link gets sucked into the belly of the beast, finding himself in a pretty unorthodox dungeon. Lord Jabu-Jabu is much bigger than he appears on the outside, and will need to navigate the twisting confines of his insides to locate Princess Ruto and a special treasure before defeating the parasite responsible for the diety fish's current state.

While the insides of Lord Jabu-Jabu may look a bit concerning, you'll soon find that the place still follows a traditional dungeon structure. This means finding ways to unlock sealed "doors", discovering Treasure Chests that contain Dungeon Maps and a Compass, and even a special tool to help you reach the end. You'll also have the secondary objective of locating the missing Princess, but when you get over how weird things look, you'll find this dungeon to be a piece of cake!

The main "entrance" room consists of Jabu-Jabu's jaws (which you can walk toward to exit the dungeon at any time, an find his mouth permanently open for easy access back inside), and a strange glowing protrusion hanging from the ceiling almost like a uvula, in front of a "door" that seems sealed.

Two Octoroks have made their home in the pools of water along his tongue, so be ready to deflect their attacks back at them, and then try hitting the ceiling protrusion with your slingshot. This will cause the far door to unseal, allowing you further inside.

Inside this next small room is a strange glowing platform, and two jellyfish-like enemies called Biri. They float fairly aimlessly unless you draw close, but are electrified and will shock you if you touch them -- even with your sword!

To make matters worse, the pellets from your Slingshot simply bounce off them, but their are a few ways to get past their electric barrier. A Deku Nut will stun the Biri, causing it to fall down and lose its electric charge. You can then follow up with a slash to kill it. Deku Sticks are also a viable alternative, as wood doesn't conduct electricity so the shock of hitting it won't affect Link!

In the next room, you'll run into Princess Ruto herself. A bit haughty and arrogant, she won't want your help if it's coming from her dad, preferring to forge off and find something she dropped herself... only to fall through an opening in the floor to the room. The area is full of such openings so you'll want to watch your step in the future, but for now follow Ruto down to floor B1.

Note that you can also take advantage of Farore's Wind to create a quick travel point at the top of the room, in case you fall down later and don't want to waste time climbing back up.

Speak to Ruto again and after insisting you want to help, she'll begrudgingly allow you the honor of carrying her through the dungeon in search of her missing "precious stone". Looking around, half of this room is blocked off -- meaning you'll eventually have to find a different way to drop down from above, but there's also another doorway by the large vines leading up to the first floor over to the southwest. You won't be able to do anything in that room yet without the right tool, so let's leave it for later.

Take Princess Ruto with you by grabbing her and holding her high over your head, and then head through the hallway to the east. On this side, you'll find several hostile floating bubbles called Shabom. They'll pop if they hit you and deal damage in the process. Like the Biri, they can't be harmed by your Slingshot, but you do have a secret weapon up your sleeve... Ruto herself!

It's a bit awkward, but you can actually toss Ruto into the bouncing bubbles like the projectile, causing them to pop without dealing any damage in the process. Ruto's great at tanking their attacks, and you don't even need to use up any of your own supplies while doing so!

In the next main room, you'll find a sunken area in the middle of the room, and several high ledges on all sides that you can't reach. Inside the pit below is something moving through the shallows, and when you leave Ruto behind for a moment to draw close, a Stinger will emerge. It'll float around in the air for a moment before dive-bombing you, but is still susceptible to your Slingshot, or you can block its attack with your shield.

When the Stingers are defeated, you can step on the glowing switch in the middle to raise the water level here. This allows you to reach a Treasure Chest on the eastern side holding the Dungeon Map!

Be sure to also check out the vines leading up to a high ledge on the western side, where you'll find a few pots stashed away next to a Gold Skulltula!

With the water raised, you'll still need a way to get Ruto across with you, so head back to where you left her sitting and step on the other glowing switch to lower the water level again. Now you can grab her and jump in the pit, and then stand on one of the raised platform to toss her to the other side, before stepping on the switch again to raise the water level so you can swim after her.

When trying to leave this room, you'll be ambushed by a new type of jellyfish, the Bari. These foes are more aggressive and much bigger than their Biri counterparts, and even split into three Biri when defeated. Since they're also electrified, using your sword is a no-go. Try using a Deku Nut to stun it, and when it splits into three Biri, consider tossing a bomb into the mix, or using Din's Fire to quickly eradicate the group!

If you played the original Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, you may remember the hassle of losing Princess Ruto if you strayed too far from her, and having to return to the previous two-tiered room to re-collect her. In the remake, she'll dutifully remain wherever you leave her sitting. You can even leave the dungeon entirely and go run some errands, and she'll be right where you left her on her return!

Head down the hall to the next narrow room, and you'll find a lone Octorok guarding another protrusion from the ceiling. Hit it with your slingshot, and the strange blue pedestal from the first room you entered will appear here, giving you a shortcut elevator back to the first floor.

Before taking Ruto and hopping on board, be sure to swim to the opposite side of the room and dive down to find an underwater passage. This leads to a lone Business Scrub, who has found a hell of a place to set up shop. Deflecting his attack back at him, he'll offer to sell you such things as more Deku Nuts and Deku Sticks to fight off electric enemies with -- or even more Business Scrub Seeds to summon merchants whenever you want.

Take the rising platform with Ruto in tow back up to the first floor 1F, and return to the room where she fell into the pit. Remembering that one part of the room was inaccessible from the rest, you'll find that the pit leading down to that area is covered in some sort of green barrier, with a connecting vein leading out the northern door.

The room is hiding several more Bari and Biri, so carefully navigate the area and consider leaving Ruto behind while you deal with immediate threats, or just run past them into the next hallway.

This next area is split into five corridors leading to circular rooms, and many of them connect to each other with more colored veins. Start by taking the first left to find a sealed door and a raised glowing switch you can plant Ruto on to keep the door open for you.

Inside this room, you'll find it full of Stinger enemies lurking in the floor. Carefully approach them one at a time to force them out of hiding, and then either snipe them down with your Slingshot, or lure them together so you can hit them all with a blast from Din's Fire. Defeating the group will reveal a large Treasure Chest, and inside is the Boomerang! With this tool, you'll be able to hit distant targets at a curved angle, and can even grab certain items and bring them back to you as the Boomerang returns!

Return to the hallway and pick up Ruto as you go to head to the main connecting corridor, which has three different colored veins leading between the rooms and back to the earlier large room. This spot is also home to several Tailpasaran - floating eel-like enemies that are electrified with a sturdy head. Since frontal assaults aren't advised, look for a secondary target on their tail to lock on using Navi, and toss your new Boomerang to swing around to their back and kill them without trouble.

The three strange colored veins are all blocking the others corridors, leaving the only open spot by following the red vein to the right, and using Ruto to open the door for you.

Inside, you'll find the source of these strange veins: colored parasitic monsters that hang down like tendrils in the middle of a circular room. They'll swing wildly forward after trembling for a moment, so lock on and keep strafing constantly. As it swings forward, look for a frayed section of the parasite near the middle, and toss your Boomerang at it to damage the parasite. You'll need to do this several times to bring the parasite down, and in doing so you'll clear away the red vein and the corridor it was blocking.

You can either leave Ruto where she is, or carry her down the left corridor following a blue vein to a room with a blue-colored parasite.

It's also flanked by several Biri, which you can either also use your Boomerang on, or toss Ruto at them. Just be sure to stay mobile, as the blue parasite will constantly be trying to smash you -- thrusting forward instead of swinging wildly.

Once you've defeated it by strafing and boomerang tossing, the corridor to the last two rooms will open up.

Be sure to check out the room on the right first that doesn't have a green vein leading to it. The room here is full of tons of Shabom bubble enemies, which your Boomerang can make quick work of by rapidly spamming it at all of them. Defeating the group will unlock a large treasure chest with a Compass inside!

Finally, head into then northern room to face the last green parasite, flanked by several Stingers. It will alternate swinging wildly, and slamming forward several times before stunning itself on the ground for a moment, giving you multiple opportunities to leap and deal damage up close, or stick with your Boomerang.

Once defeated, the final vein will disintegrate, meaning the barrier back in the two-tiered room full of pits is now gone. Take Ruto with you and head back, and make a beeline for for blue opening.

It's worth making a Farore's Wind point either above or on the new ledge you drop down onto from the second floor. From this ledge, first look to the north where some Biri float around to spot a Gold Skulltula along the wall. Using your Boomerang, you can now both hit it from a distance, and recover the Skull Token using your Boomerang!

You should also jump down to the lower floor, and take the door to the southwest. There's a strange undulating platform here that will attack you if you try to jump to it, but throwing your Boomerang at it first will freeze it in place, allowing you to jump across to break several pots and open a small Treasure Chest with a Red Rupee inside.

Warp back to the high ledge where you dropped down with Ruto from the floor above, and head down the hall toward the room to the northwest. This small corridor also has another Gold Skulltula hiding along the ceiling, which you can dislodge with your Boomerang and claim its token.

As you enter the next room, Princess Ruto will spy her special stone on the high platform in front of you, and demand you get her over to it. Dutifully toss Ruto onto the platform and she'll claim the Spiritual Stone of Water... wait that was your job!

Before she has a chance to celebrate, the high platform will suddenly rise up, and upon its return you'll be face to giant face with a Big Octo!

The giant cephalopod spans the entire width of the narrow circular path around the central platform, and its only weak spot appears to be green growth on its back. It'll charge relentlessly forward, but you can stun it by hitting it with your Boomerang.

Once you do, sprint around to its back to see the exposed weak point. It will likely regain its movement and try to scuttle off while hiding the growth, but you can toss your Boomerang again while in pursuit to stun it once more, and then jump attack the weak point to deal some lasting damage.

After hitting it several times, the Big Octo will spin around and burrow out of sight, leaving you to deal with several Shabom bubbles it leaves behind. Quickly take out any that are nearby, and then pan your camera around to spot where the Big Octo resurfaces.

Let it try and charge you once more and then stun it with the Boomerang once it gets in range, and repeat the process of running around to attack from behind while keeping it stunned. Do this three times, and the giant beast will be defeated.

You can now take the lowered platform up to go find Princess Ruto somewhere on the second floor 2F. There's some pots here to replenish your items, and a corridor leading to a room to the south.

This area has two more of the wildly swinging "platforms" in the water that don't want you crossing. Like the optional room, you can hit both with a Boomerang to stun them for several moments, giving you time to get across.

In this next room, there's a sealed door with a switch nearby, but you're missing your personal switch presser Zora Princess. Instead, look for a trail of small platforms leading down to the lower part of the room, and you'll find a small portable stone block down here. It's not Princess Ruto, but it will have to do. Jump across the first platform and then toss it ahead of you to the main upper platform before climbing up the vines yourself. Place it on the switch, and continue on.

The watery area beyond has a few floating Biri, a sealed door, and a very tall pillar with vines on the back side. There's a dangling protrusion high up in the ceiling, but its protected by barriers straight on that prevents hitting it with a Slingshot.

Look around to the backside of the tall pillar, and along the vines leading up to the top, you can find the last Gold Skulltula to claim in this dungeon with a shot from your Boomerang or Slingshot!

Upon climbing to the top of the high pillar, you'll have a roundabout line of sight to the protected protrusion nearby. Even if you can't hit it directly, you can still have Navi target the object, and then toss your Boomerand to slide around the side of the barrier to hit it, opening the door below.

There's a few pots to replenish lost items here, and when you're ready, head through to find the source of this infection inside Jabu-Jabu that's kidnapped Princess Ruto.

The darkened arena you find yourself will flash with bioluminescent light as the Bioelectric Anemone known as Barinade arrives. The strange creatures has covered itself in barbed jellyfish that it tethers to itself, while lightning-emitting proboscis protect the tendrils that tether it to the ceiling.

As long as those lightning emitters are active, you'll want to constantly be moving, strafing the strange creature and dodging the lightning blasts they'll send your way regularly. Your first order of business should be finding a way to reveal Barinade's vulnerabilities.

Just like the parasite veins you fought with earlier, the tethers keeping the creature to the ceiling all have frayed points along the top, and you can alternate between the three tethers to toss your Boomerang at while strafing, taking them out one at a time while evading incoming lightning blasts.

Once Barinade is completely untethered from the ceiling, phase two will begin. Barinade will dislodge the electric jellyfish guarding its body, and send them spinning around in front as a moving electrified shield. You don't want to come into contact with this offensive shield, so keep your distance as it starts to move around the arena.

Unfortunately, the energy Barinade emits keeps the electrified jellyfish shielded from your own attacks, and its abdomen is similarly protected from both your sword and ranged attacks. Instead, you'll need to play this part entirely defensively, using the breadth of the arena to keep away, or looking for a gap to dart between the jellies. If you watch, the extended output will make Barinade's core burn brightly, until eventually it shorts out. This will cause the shields to be removed for a moment, leaving the jellyfish it used as a barrier to become defenseless.

Waste no time in charging in to slice apart as many blobby creatures as you can to diminish its barrier, before Barinade can restart its power. It won't reactivate its shield immediately, but it will start to target you with its lightning blast, so keep your attacks quick and short as you stay mobile.

You may have to stun Barinade twice using this method to clear out all of its shielded jelly surrounding it. Be patient, and if you get run over or electrocuted, be sure to run the length of the arena's outer wall to find pots to replenish your health. Once all the blobby shields have been sliced away, you'll be in the third phase.

At this point all Barinade will raise its exposed abdomen out from its hiding spot under the floor, bringing with it the final group of electrified jellyfish to keep you at bay. This time, its core is no longer protected from attacks, but it will change things up by not only keeping its blobby barriers close to it, but also turning its exposed abdomen purple as it charges you quickly. Ditch the targeting and sprint to the side to avoid its charges, and then wait for the jellyfish to stop spinning quickly.

Line up a shot and hit the abdomen, which will cause it to sink into the ground, and leave the jelly defenseless. Like before, quickly dash in and cut or boomerang the unguarded blobby creatures until it has no left.

In a last ditch effort, Barinade will now fully sprout out of the ground, flying around the room and emitting lightning blasts in all directions. Stay mobile, and get in close before hitting its exposed weak spot with a Boomerang. This will cause it to sink to the ground, and now that its weak spot is exposed you can unleash some jump and spin attacks to deal major damage.

Keep up the assault, pull back when it burrows under to dodge lightning blast, then refocus your attack when it tries to take to the air again. After 2 or three stuns, you'll be able to carve up Barinade into little pieces, and earn a new Heart Container for your trouble!

Head into the blue light once you've claimed your health upgrade to find an impatient Princess Ruto, and you'll be transported outside. Now that's she's cooled down her temper, Ruto will find Link a pretty interesting guy, and agree to give him a gift meant for the man who would be her husband one day - the Zora Sapphire.

With all three Spiritual Stones collected, all that's left to open the way to the Sacred Realm is returning to Hyrule Castle to meet with Princess Zelda. However, gaining the Boomerang means you have a few new things you can do, and it's worth seeking them out before making our way back to the castle.

To start, be sure to play the Sun's Song here in Zora Fountain. Look for a nearby archway in the water you can climb up, and on the far wall, a Gold Skulltula will appear at night, and you can toss your Boomerang to collect its token.

Next, make your way back through Zora's Domain, speaking to the King and the other Zoras to hear some praise, and then travel back downriver toward Hyrule Field. At this point, you'll want to stop in by the Bean Seller, and if you have the funds, buy at least 7 of Magic Seeds -- we've got planting to do!

As you re-enter Hyrule Field, look out in the distance, and you should spot a strange man running along the field alone. Try to catch up to him (or wait for nightfall when he usually stops and sits by a boulder), and he'll tell you of his desire to run with the winds, and how once upon a time rabbits used to race across these fields. If you wear the Bunny Hood that the Happy Mask Shop rents out in front of him, he'll plead with you to sell it to him, and buy it for a whopping 200 Rupees, meaning you'll earn 150 in profit! You can watch as the running man takes off with his new Bunny Hood at incredible speeds. What a happy customer.

As long as your traversing Hyrule Field, be sure to stop by Lon Lon Ranch. Now armed with your Boomerang, check out the main house just by the racetrack entrance at night, and you can find a Gold Skulltula hiding on a window that you can defeat and grab its token with your Boomerang.

You should also enter the crumbling tower in the southwest corner of the ranch at night, the one that was hiding a Piece of Heart. Look up for a high ledge with vines you can't quite reach, but your Boomerang can reach the Gold Skulltula skittering around above and nab its token.

By now, you will have noticed dark clouds gathering around the entrance to Hyrule Castle Town. For some strange reason, the drawbridge is up for the first time ever...

As Link approaches, his prophetic dream will come to pass. The drawbridge will lower as Zelda and Impa race back. The Princess will barely have time to toss something toward you before disappearing, leaving you face to face with Ganondorf, King of the Gerudo.

Seemingly unbothered by Link's attempt at heroism, Ganondorf will blast him aside before giving chase, leaving you to find what it was Zelda tried to give you. Check the moat for a shining blue object, and you'll recover the fabled Ocarina of Time!

As you do, Link will be granted a vision from the Princess. Knowing she wouldn't be able to speak to you in person, she's left you the Ocarina, and a special melody used to open the door in the Temple of Time:

Complete the prompt to learn the Song of Time, a powerful melody that is the key to unlocking the Sacred Realm!

While time is most certainly of the essence... it wouldn't hurt to wait until you're fully prepared to opening that Door of Time, right? You can now head into Hyrule Castle Town to find the whole town abuzz having witnessed Zelda fleeing from Ganondorf. Dark times are surely coming, but there's one thing you should do here first.

Now that you've sold the Bunny Hood to the running man in Hyrule Field, return to pay the Happy Mask Salesman the 50 Rupees, while keeping the rest for yourself. You'll have officially completed all his tasks, and in addition to unlocking all previous masks to wear, you can also rent out masks of Gorons, Zora, and Gerudo for fun, and a special Mask of Truth that has mystical effects!

When speaking to most people, you'll get an additional bit of dialogue as you hear the person's very thoughts! You can also use the Mask of Truth when interacting with all the strange Sheikah Stones across Hyrule to learn random trivia and tips!

Head back to Kakariko Village next. Now that you have over 30 Gold Skulltulas, you can stop by the Cursed Spider House for your next reward: the Giant's Wallet. With this, you'll be able to stockpile as much as 1,000 Rupees!

Next, head into the Graveyard at night. Look behind Dampe's cabin, and you'll find another Gold Skulltula waiting for you on a high wall. Now with your Boomerang, you'll be able to defeat it and claim its token.

This means the Cursed Spider house will have yet another reward for you: 20 Bombchus!

This is also a good time to do some Magic Bean planting. There's a patch of soft soil over by the lone tree on the north side of the graveyard. Similarly, you can make the hike up the Death Mountain Trail, and plant some more Magic Beans at the soil just outside Dodongo's Cavern.

Be sure you've picked up the Mask of Truth before returning to the Lost Woods. First, you'll want to stop off in the area under the bridge leading out of the Kokiri Forest to find the soft soil you found a spider in, and plant some more Magic Beans.

There's another spot in the hidden grove full of Deku Business Scrubs (head north from the Zora River shortcut, then west), and plant the beans in the soil by the tree.

Drop down into the Grotto here to find the Forest Stage. If you didn't already get the reward for going on stage with the Skull Mask, be sure to do that, and you can also display the Mask of Truth here to be awarded a second Deku Nut Bag!

We haven't really been to the Gerudo Valley yet, and there's a reason for that. The secretive home of the Gerudo Tribe isn't allowing any visitors, and their large bridge has a guard who won't let anyone pass. Now that we have a few upgrades, it's worth stopping by to get everything we can. When you approach a small wooden plank over a pool of water, be sure to play the Sun's Song to turn day to night. Soon, a Golden Skulltula will emerge under the bridge, and you can hop down to defeat it and claim its token.

Though you can't cross the bridge, there are sections of the valley wall you can jump to, and along the opposite side you can spy a large Treasure Chest. The gap is normally too big to cross, but there happens to be a Cucco nearby that you can grab and float across the valley to the other side. Open the Treasure Chest, and you'll find a Piece of Heart inside!

With the Cucco still around, grab it and look down at the bottom of the valley with the raging river below that feeds out to Lake Hylia. Jump off with the Cucco and slowly float down to a large alcove along the waterline.

It's here you'll find a lone Gerudo tending to her cow, and she's far less hostile than the guard above (you can even play Epona's Song to get some free milk. Nearby is the last patch of soft soil you can find for the moment, so plant your last bit of Magic Beans, and then drop a Bug in to make another Gold Skulltula pop out.

Finally, head up this large alcove path up north toward the giant waterfall. You'll find there's actually a path behind the waterfall, and you can climb it to reach another Piece of Heart!

From here, it's best that you hop into the river, and let it carry you into Lake Hylia. Now that you've got the Boomerang, head up to the Observatory and start walking across the rope bridge. Play the Sun's Song to turn day to night, and look back to spot a Gold Skulltula just out of reach, that you can now retrieve the token from with your Boomerang.

When you're ready, have Kaepora Gaebora give you a lift back to Hyrule Castle.

At this point, you'll have accomplished everything you can possibly do before opening the Door of Time, this means:

Having 18 Pieces of Heart (for a total of 10 Heart Containers)

Fully Upgraded Deku Stick / Deku Nut / Deku Seed / Bomb Bags

Din's Fire, Farore's Wind, and the Improved Spin Attack

Now that you're prepared, enter the Temple of Time, and play the Song of Time in front of the inscription. The Spiritual Stones will fly to their designated slots, and the mighty slab will open.

Take the new pathway to a chamber that holds the legendary blade of evil's bane: The Master Sword. Pulling this sword out is the final key to opening the Sacred Realm, but as it turns out, that's exactly what someone else has been waiting for.

When next Link awakens, much will have changed, and things will have gotten much more dire in the land of Hyrule .

articles.body:
Welcome to IGN's guide to All Gossip Stone Locations in The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake. Just like the original game, these Gossip Stones are hidden all over the game, telling the time and giving out tips.

Check out IGN's complete guide to Gossip Stones below:

Gossip Stones are these strange rocks with the Sheikah Symbol on their face. Hitting them causes them to tell the time, but they can do many other things:

Speaking to one while wearing the Mask of Truth gets you a unique "secret" from each Stone. We've included them all below.

Playing Zelda's Lullaby, Epona's Song, Song of Storms, or Song of Time in front of one gets you a full health and magic restore.

Hitting them with random gear, such as Hookshot, Megaton Hammer, Bombs, and Din's Fire, will result in all different reactions. Try them out!

The first Gossip Stone you are likely to encounter. This one is located on the north side cliff in Kokiri Forest, near the Lost Woods entrance.

Secret: "They say one of the children living among the Kokiri left the confines of their forest home - and has somehow survived."

The next two Gossip Stones are found outisde of the Great Deku Tree dungeon. Look north of the dungeon entrance to see this one among the roots.

Secret: "If what they say is true, one of the fairy children living within Kokiri Forest isn't actually a fairy child."

Then go a little further north to see the next Gossip Stone up against the back rock wall.

Secret: "Apparently the traditional Kokiri dialect includes frequent use of "yaha," but they rarely speak that way these days. Yaha!"

Go left, then left from the Lost Woods entrance, then go straight ahead under the bridge to find this Gossip Stone next to a Business Scrub at the dead end.

Secret: "Stories say that outsiders who enter the forest of the Kokiri are doomed to become monsters."

This Gossip Stone is found at the far end of Sacred Grove, near Saria. Check the southwest corner of the room.

Secret: "Despite appearances, it seems Saria is often lonely."

The next two Gossip Stones are found on top of the Sacred Grove maze. Once you have made it through the maze, you can find a latter at the end to get up on top which serves out a shortcut out. The first Gossip Stone is up against the west wall.

Secret: "They say the size of the owl Kaepora Gaebora may make him appear a bit grandiose, but he's actually rather lighthearted."

The second Gossip Stone is closer to the exit door, toward the southeast corner.

Secret: "Wisdom says our past may not always be behind us nor our future always before."

This Gossip Stone is found in the grotto at the far end of Sacred Grove, near Saria. Use a Bomb to blow up the rock in the southeast corner of the room.

Secret: "There are whispers that if you hold out a Deku stick and slowly approach a nearby butterfly, you may get a surprise."

These four Gossip Stones are lined up just outside of the Temple of Time. Their Secrets, left to right:

Secret 1: "Word around town is that the operator of the Shooting Gallery doesn't have much patience for rule breakers."

Secret 2: "Some suggest that using vision-enhanced lenses should be banned at the Treasure-Chest Shop in Hyrule Town."

Secret 3: "Legend has it the owl Kaepora Gaebora is the reincarnation of an ancient sage."

Secret 4: "Apparently, playing certain combinations of musical notes to gossip stones can produce some marvelous results."

This Gossip Stone is at the top of the vines you climb to sneak into Hyrule Castle. Find him next to the large tree.

Secret: "They say Ganondorf rides a pitch-black Gerudo stallion."

This Gossip Stone is found in the courtyard in front of Hyrule Castle, just after you climb the stone wall to get out of the garden.

Secret: "The chatter around Hyrule Castle suggests Princess Zelda is actually quite the tomboy."

This Gossip Stone is found in the large central room of Dodongo's Cavern. Find it in the northeast corner.

Secret: "They say the hardness of a rock roast determines its flavor."

This Gossip Stone is found in Medigoron's room, which is accessible once you have Bombs. Blow up the rocks blocking the tunnel in the southeast corner of the top floor.

Secret: "They say Medigoron can eat, sleep, and maintain a normal life without ever leaving the confines of his cramped shop."

This Gossip Stone is found in the storage room on the top floor, west side of Goron City. Use Bombs to blow up the rocks blocking the way and make your way to the back of the room where the Stone is waiting with some chests.

Secret: "They say there are some goodies stashed away in the large vessel standing in the heart of Goron City."

This Gossip Stone is found very near the summit of Death Mountain, on the last platform before you reach the Great Fairy Fountain and Biggoron.

Secret: "Word is that changing the Targeting Type in Options to Toggle can make it easier to fight large groups."

This Gossip Stone is in a grotto en route to the Death Mountain Summit. It is just after the cliff section where you need Bombs to clear the path. You will also need a Bomb to blow up the rock blocking the grotto entrance.

Secret: "Apparently, you can make new discoveries when returning to a dungeon, even if you've completed it before."

This Gossip Stone is found in the southeast corner of Death Mountain Crater, to the right if you are entering via the Death Mountain Summit tunnel.

Secret: "I've heard you should keep flames away from stones like me! Who knows what could happen!"

articles.title: GTA 6 Will Run at 30fps On All Consoles, Features Ray Tracing Improvements on PS5 Pro
articles.summary: Rockstar has finally announced performance for GTA 6. It’ll run at 30fps on all consoles, but PS5 Pro enhancements that improve ray tracing.
articles.body:
Rockstar has finally announced performance for GTA 6 . It’ll run at 30fps on all consoles, but PS5 Pro enhancements improve ray tracing.

“Grand Theft Auto VI has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits to bring the vast and rich world of Leonida to life — while maintaining the density and visual fidelity of all its environments and inhabitants,” Rockstar said in a post.

That means no matter what console you play on — PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X, or Xbox Series S — the game will run at, or below, 30fps. “Targeting 30fps” is different to locked 30fps, so there’s likely some fluctuation in busy scenes.

Ray tracing allows for finer detail in shadows, as well as shadows that naturally blur and widen the farther away they get from the object casting them, matching the physical size of the light source. Improvements here are only available on PS5 Pro.

There are also some PlayStation exclusive details in the controls, which support high-fidelity haptic feedback on the DualSense controller — Rockstar says it “fully integrated” this into the game. The same goes for Sony’s Tempest 3D audio for spatial sound improvements.

Those last two are true for both base PS5 and PS5 Pro. All this and improved load times make “Grand Theft Auto VI play best on PlayStation 5 consoles,” according to Rockstar.

GTA 6 will also be available to play via Xbox’s Cloud Gaming on all Xbox consoles, including Xbox One, surprisingly. The game will utilize Xbox Series S graphics settings, however.

There are no details about how the game runs on Xbox Series S, but it’s widely expected to be the inferior version of the game due to the lower hardware specs of the console.

“As with all cloud streaming, connection speeds and other technical factors may influence game performance in ways that would not impact local gameplay,” Rockstar said.

You’ll also be able to play GTA 6 on Remote Play on both PlayStation and Xbox consoles when it launches on November 19.

articles.title: You Don't Need a Current-Gen Console if You're Happy to Play GTA 6 at Xbox Series S Settings
articles.summary: After months of speculation, Rockstar finally revealed that GTA 6 would be targeting 30fps on all of the current-generation consoles, including the Xbox Series S. But, thanks to a cloud streaming deal with Xbox, you can technically play the game on the Xbox One.
articles.body:
After months of speculation, Rockstar finally revealed that GTA 6 would be targeting 30fps on all of the current-generation consoles , including the Xbox Series S . But, thanks to a cloud streaming deal with Xbox, you can technically play the game on the Xbox One.

While GTA 6 will only be running locally on the PS5 and Xbox Series consoles, Rockstar finally detailed which devices will be able to use Xbox Cloud Gaming to play the game. Its blog post says, "The game will also be available via Xbox Cloud Gaming on Xbox Series X|S and Xbox One consoles, utilizing Xbox Series S graphics settings." So, you can technically play GTA 6 on the Xbox One, which launched all the way back in 2013, it just won't be, well, running on the Xbox One itself.

We've known for a while that GTA 6 would be playable via Xbox Cloud Gaming, after an exclusive deal was announced in October. At the time, because of the wide swath of devices that can use Xbox Cloud Gaming, this deal fueled speculation that you'd be able to play GTA 6 on everything from a gaming PC to an iPhone. However, Xbox Chief Strategy Officer Matthew Ball later clarified that the game wouldn't be streaming to PC. But, now, thanks to Rockstar's blog, we now know the full extent of devices that can stream GTA 6.

The real catch to streaming GTA 6 is going to be the quality. According to the blog, the streaming version will be running at the same graphics settings as the Xbox Series S version, which is the weakest current-gen system. It's not clear yet what the game will look like running on the Series S, but Rockstar did say that it was targeting 30fps on all of the consoles.

It's likely that the Xbox Series S version of GTA 6 will be running at a lower resolution, though, which is probably the reason why Rockstar opted for that version of the game being used for streaming. Due to the immense demand that this game has, it's likely that a ton of people are going to be trying to stream this game at launch, and opting for the lowest resolution version means less risk of Microsoft's servers buckling under the weight.

If you do want to play GTA 6 this way, though, keep in mind that Xbox Cloud Gaming comes with its own list of caveats. You're at the mercy of your internet connection and Microsoft's servers, and could deal with graphics artifacts due to bandwidth issues, lag, or just getting booted out of the game if the servers go down. Plus, Microsoft's limits to Xbox Cloud Gaming went live this month, so even if you have a Game Pass Ultimate subscription, you'll be limited to 15 hours of game tim e before you have to buy more.

If you are going to play GTA 6 locally on your own console, you might want to save a nice chunk of storage for it, as it's going to take up 212GB of space . With a game that big, you're going to want to preload it if you want to play right when the game goes live too, and luckily preloads just went live this morning .

After being announced last month, PlayStation’s new 'Prism Collection' of DualSense controllers and PS5 covers is officially up for preorder.

The controllers have a list price of $84.99 and are available from a number of retailers ( see them at Amazon ), while the matching PS5 covers are listed for $74 exclusively from PlayStation Direct . The Prism Collection includes three new DualSense controllers and three matching PS5 covers. With the new design, PlayStation’s team was aiming "to bring back the iconic see-through trend of the late '90s in a fresh, modern way" while giving players a closer look at the inner workings of the best PS5 controller. Xbox is also going retro with its X25 Special Edition console , so the transparent trend seems to back in full force.

PlayStation's specific take on the design still maintains some classic Sony sleekness. A high-gloss clear finish covers most of the controller, with a metallic finish on the middle cover. The three specific colorways are interestingly named, to say the least, owing to the funky color effects of the translucent shell. The Emerald Green and Graphite Grey colors both clearly have some blue in there, while Flare Orange looks entirely red to me. I don’t know if this is a white/gold blue/black dress situation or what, but I’d take a hard look at the images for a clearer sense of each design.

Otherwise, you’re looking at a classic DualSense controller (check out our original 9/10 review ), complete with a built-in mic, haptic feedback, and adaptive triggers. In addition to being built for PS5, the wireless controllers are also compatible with Mac, PC, and mobile devices.

If you're generally in the market for a new PS5 controller, you have tons of options , but there's one in particular I'd recommend taking a look at. PlayStation is releasing two special GTA 6 edition DualSense controllers alongside the game’s impending launch on November 19. (Yes, it's that close .)

While the new Prism Collection will likely stay on the market for the foreseeable future, limited edition controllers like the GTA 6 edition tend to sell out and never come back.

articles.title: PlayStation Plus PC App Will Go Offline December 10, as Sony Continues to Retreat From PC
articles.summary: Outside of the few games that Sony has ported to Windows, the PlayStation Plus app on PC was the best way to play PS5 games on PC, even if you had to stream them. But now, Sony will be retiring the PlayStation Plus PC app.
articles.body:
Outside of the few games that Sony has ported to Windows, the PlayStation Plus app on PC was the best way to play PS5 games on PC, even if you had to stream them. But now, Sony will be retiring the PlayStation Plus PC app .

In a blog post today , Sony announced that the PlayStation Plus app is going away on December 10 in order to focus on console users. Sony justified the decision by saying, "With a very small number of eligible PlayStation Plus Premium members (less than 0.4%) using the PlayStation Plus app on PC, making this change allows us to focus on enhancing high-quality experiences that more of our members want to use. As a result, the PlayStation Plus cloud streaming app on PC will no longer be available."

This comes just a few months after Sony backed out of releasing PC ports of PlayStation exclusives, instead opting to keep its single-player games exclusive to its own consoles. Even the reasoning is similar, with Sony Interactive Entertainment CEO Herman Hulst telling employees that Sony's PC ports were 'inconsistent' and didn't make enough money .

However, with the PlayStation Plus app on PC going away, it's going to be a bit harder to stream games when you're away from your console, something you can easily do from your phone or PC with an Xbox Game Pass subscription – unless it's GTA 6 , of course. With this change, the only streaming option for PS5 outside of a console is Remote Play, and that requires a console to be on the same network.

It's also worth mentioning that consoles are only getting more expensive, and the PS5 Pro will still set you back $1,559 at the time of writing on Amazon . As hardware gets more expensive, cloud streaming is going to be increasingly more important, and it seems like Sony is backing away from it – if even just a little bit.

Sony has avoided putting the same limitations on cloud gaming that other companies have, though. Just this month, Microsoft implemented a time limit on Xbox Cloud Streaming, limiting Game Pass Ultimate subscribers to just 15 hours of play time before they need to break out their wallets to buy extra time. Nvidia's GeForce Now also has time limits, but they're a bit more liberal, allowing 100 hours of playtime each month.
