articles.title: GTA 6 Was Never Going to Hit 60 Frames per Second on Consoles
articles.summary: Back when Rockstar showed off a bunch of GTA 6 gameplay on Netflix, one thing was incredibly clear – the game was running around 30 fps. And now that Rockstar has confirmed that it is targeting 30 fps on every console, including the PS5 Pro, it's clear that the game likely never would have run at a solid 60 on console.
articles.body:
Back when Rockstar showed off a bunch of GTA 6 gameplay on Netflix, one thing was incredibly clear: The game was running around 30fps. And now that Rockstar has confirmed that it is targeting 30fps on every console, including the PS5 Pro, it's clear that the game likely never would have run at a solid 60 on console.

In a blog post today, Rockstar finally shared some performance information, saying it was targeting 30fps on every console, with the PS5 Pro instead getting some extra ray tracing and PSSR to make it look better. While I'm sure there are plenty of people who would rather that effort go into a 'performance mode' that runs a bit faster, it might not have even been possible.

The biggest difference between all of the different levels of consoles, the Xbox Series S, the base PS5 and Xbox Series S, and the PS5 Pro is the strength of the GPU. That's why the PS5 Pro is getting ray tracing effects that the other consoles aren't. But, with an open world game like GTA 6, the limiting factor is probably the CPU.

Rockstar has already gone on record saying that the map in GTA 6 is bigger than any other game from the developer, and that, specifically, it's going to be densely populated. When we interviewed Rob Nelson , co-studio head of Rockstar North, he told us the team was "doing everything we possibly can to create the largest, deepest, most densely populated and complex world we have ever built for people to get lost in." And no matter how much trickery you can pull with a GPU, simulating an entire city full of NPCs is going to tax the CPU.

Just watching the Netflix extended trailer , and there are a lot of people in every scene, each of which needs to be simulated by the CPU. But, due to the nature of GTA, it's more than just individual scenes having a lot of people wandering around. This is an open world game, where you can get in a car and traverse the entire map at high speeds. The game needs to be able to account for this and load in new actors dynamically, and there's only so much you can do with an 8-core Zen 2 CPU at a 3.85GHz boost clock.

Remember, too, that on every current-gen console, the CPU and GPU share a unified memory pool. That really matters in a game like GTA 6 because that memory has to handle both simulation data like NPCs and detailed weather events, along with graphics data like textures, lighting and character meshes. No one outside of Rockstar has seen the performance metrics for this game, but I wouldn't be surprised if the game is running up against its limits on all four of the consoles.

As it stands, the only way you're going to be able to play this game at 60fps is to either wait for the PC version or the inevitable PS6 and Project Helix ports. But, I think even most gaming PCs are going to struggle to get a solid 60fps in this game.

If you look at the most recent Steam Hardware Survey, most people are on CPUs with 8-cores or less, which could run into some of the same limits as the console versions. The difference, though, is that most PCs have dedicated RAM and VRAM for their CPU and GPU, respectively, so there should be less of a bottleneck – especially if you're on a speedy X3D processor with all of that speedy cache available. At least it looks like I probably don't have to wait too long to see how GTA 6 is going to run on PC .

Only time will tell just how well GTA 6 is going to run on these consoles, and hopefully it stays locked at a solid 30fps most of the time. Rockstar probably chose its words very carefully when it said it was 'targeting' 30fps in its blog, so I'm very curious at how well the Xbox Series S is going to hold up. Now that we're just 9 days out from GTA 6's November 19 release date, we won't have to wait long to find out.

The sequel to the first Death Stranding game, this follow-up takes eleven months after the events of its predecessor, featuring Sam Porter Bridges and Fragile as they set out across Australia to connect surviving colonies with the Chiral Network. articles.title: Someone Got Halo 1 Running on a Sega Dreamcast
articles.summary: A developer has successfully gotten the original Halo: Combat Evolved, a day-one launch title for the original Xbox in 2001, ported and running on the Sega Dreamcast – in both campaign and multiplayer. And they've posted 28 minutes of gameplay footage from the campaign and multiplayer to prove it.
articles.body:
A developer has successfully gotten the original Halo: Combat Evolved, a day-one launch title for the original Xbox in 2001, ported and running on the Sega Dreamcast – in both campaign and multiplayer. And he's posted 28 minutes of gameplay footage from the campaign and multiplayer to prove it.

X user and game developer "Jilted Valkyrie" uploaded the footage just days ahead of the 25th anniversary of both Halo and the Xbox itself. The Dreamcast, meanwhile, is a tad older, having launched in Japan in late 1998 and worldwide in late 1999. The footage shows a modified title screen displaying the title, "Halo: Dreamcast Evolved," with the legendary Halo theme music playing. It then shows multiplayer footage on a number of maps, including big ones like Sidewinder. Meanwhile, footage from the first mission of the campaign is there too. The framerate appears to dip below 30fps at times, but it doesn't take away from the technical marvel that is getting an Xbox game running on the older Dreamcast hardware.

Jilted Valkyrie says the campaign port is currently 77% complete, and he shouts out Dreamcast developer Falco Girgis for his help on the project. "If you like what you see, go give @falco_girgis a follow. Without his work in KOS and SH4ZAM, this unique, passionate port of Halo would not exist. He inspired me with his technical posts on GTA3 for Dreamcast to do something I always wondered about... Halo on Sega."

He later added, "It's not a 1:1 port, so the experience has completely new things to it not in any other version. There's even an entire new mode... plus who wouldn't want to play Halo online on Dreamcast?" He did not give details on the new mode, however. Finally, he says that he expects to release it this year.

As for modern Halo, Xbox seems set to reboot the franchise – or at the very least, the way Halo is made. Xbox leadership took development duties on the next mainline Halo away from Halo Studios (nee 343 Industries) and handed them to Activision , who will form a new team to helm the project. It's a bold move, and it remains to be seen if it can restore the series to its former glory .

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

articles.title: PlayStation Cancels Live-Service Heist Shooter, Fairgames
articles.summary: Fairgames, a live-service heist game from PlayStation's Haven Studios, has been canceled by Sony.
articles.body:
Fairgames , a live-service heist game from PlayStation's Haven Studios, has been canceled by Sony.

A new report from Bloomberg reveals that Fairgames has been scrapped, three and a half years after its announcement. Developer Haven Studios will not be shut down, nor will there be any layoffs, as PlayStation has decided to turn the team into a support studio for other first-party projects. The decision to pull the plug on the game was made after a recent test did not meet internal expectations.

“While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” said executives Sean Decker and John Doyle in a note reviewed by Bloomberg. “Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.”

The test being referenced here is likely one that made some waves earlier this fall. A mysterious game known as Project Espresso, which looked a lot like Fairgames, began advertising private playtests with a gameplay trailer back in September . Not much is known about those tests, but they didn't seem to be very fruitful for the team.

Fairgames was announced in 2023 and has been the subject of scrutiny for some time. Some fans pushed back on PlayStation's live-service pivot during the early 2020s, as the company has always excelled with blockbuster single-player games. When Concord bombed , fans began to express even further revulsion toward titles like Fairgames. The project has also been soured by a number of setbacks, including departures of key developers and internal struggles .

Fairgames' cancelation marks yet another major failure for PlayStation's live-service efforts. Concord flopped, The Last of Us Online was scrapped , an online God of War game was killed , and Marathon has been struggling since launch. Helldivers 2, on the other hand, has been a big win for PlayStation. There's some hope that maybe Bungie's decision to revive Destiny 2 could be productive , but Sony seems to be moving away from live-service. The only other major live-service game from PlayStation on the horizon is 4:Loop , a new game from JJ Abrams' studio, Bad Robot. We'll see if it suffers a similar fate as these other titles.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: World of Warcraft Forever Hotfix Will Thin Out Overcrowded Zones and Help Faction Balance
articles.summary: World of Warcraft Forever has been incredibly popular, and has gone down as the biggest WoW launch in history. It's little wonder then, that some zones are absolutely packed with players. And, Blizzard has implemented a fix.
articles.body:
World of Warcraft Forever has been incredibly popular, and has gone down as the biggest WoW launch in history. It's little wonder, then, that some zones are absolutely packed with players — but thankfully, Blizzard has implemented a fix.

In a hotfix last night , Blizzard lowered the population in overcrowded zones, which should give players more of a chance to get quests done without competing with a hundred other players to tag a spider. In the developers' notes, Blizzard also noted that "We’ve made this an even bigger change on the PvP ruleset, following feedback from players that they felt overcrowded in several places. We will continue to monitor how zones feel and make further adjustments as necessary."

Unlike past versions of WoW, which had a variety of servers available, World of Warcraft Forever has one server that's divided into different rulesets: PvP, PvE, RPPvP, RP and Hardcore. Instead of dividing players among different servers, Blizzard uses layering to group people into different instances of the world. And because WoW Forever's whole thing is being surrounded by other players, Blizzard seemingly opted to try and get as many people into each layer as possible without causing problems.

However, while it's fun to see hundreds of players running around each zone, this approach has caused some issues. Some people on the PvE rulesets have reported difficulties in being able to finish quests, especially in the earlier zones, as they have to compete with dozens of different players to get anything done. But the problem is especially bad for players in the PvP rulesets because of a faction imbalance.

At least here in the US, The Horde is much more popular than The Alliance, and that's causing problems. For Alliance players, they're outnumbered when they're questing in the world, which means they get killed instantly in later zones. For Horde players, they can't create new toons, because Blizzard is throttling character creation to try and preserve faction balance.

Blizzard Community Manager Kaivax has addressed this in a seperate note last night , saying, "It’s vitally important that the PvP rulesets in WoW: Forever have balanced factions where both factions vie for supremacy, creating memories of epic victories and stunning defeats that we all remember for years to come. While even the most extreme case in a region is currently at roughly a 55/45 split, that is not as close as we want it to be." Blizzard wants to get that balance as close to 50/50 as possible.

To address the matter, Kaivax says, "In the short term, that means that it will become increasingly difficult to create characters on the more populous faction in each region – currently Horde on North American PvP rulesets or Alliance in EU Roleplay-PvP. As everyone settles and shifts, these may flip to the other side."

Despite some of these growing pains, though, World of Warcraft Forever is still proving to be one of the smoothest launches in Blizzard history. Launch night went off without a hitch , thanks to the servers running on around 251TB of RAM and over 70,000 CPU cores.

articles.title: DC's New Leader Will Reportedly Prioritize More Well-Known Characters Like Batman and Wonder Woman, Reboot Has Yet to Be Decided
articles.summary: DC Studios' new boss is reportedly planning to prioritize more mainstream characters like Batman and Wonder Woman going forward.
articles.body:
DC Studios' new boss is reportedly planning to prioritize more mainstream characters like Batman and Wonder Woman going forward.

Earlier this week, it was announced that DC Studios heads James Gunn and Peter Safran were stepping down (reports indicate they were actually fired ), and now... we have an idea of what the new direction for the franchise may look like.

According to a new report from The Wrap , DC Studios' new incoming CEO, Jeremy Latcham, is expected to focus only on the hits going forward. The report claims that Latcham has been tasked by Skydance CEO David Ellison to assemble the Justice League on the big screen as quickly as possible. That means prioritizing projects with The Flash, Wonder Woman, Batman, and other heroes that the average filmgoer would recognize.

9 DC Graphic Novels You Should Read to Understand James Gunn's DCU

As a result, don't expect bigger swings with more niche characters like Clayface, Booster Gold, or Peacemaker. The report even name-checked "modest" characters like Supergirl as not being a focus going forward.

As of right now, DC has yet to decide if they will need to wipe the slate clean again and do a full reboot, with new actors and storylines. The universe is still so young and has yet to interconnect with all of its installments, so there's room to pivot... and it would be a PR disaster to recast David Corenswet after also publicly dumping Henry Cavill just a few years ago .

The focus on mainstream characters is the direct inverse of James Gunn's style, as he really rose in prominence with Guardians of the Galaxy, a film about a group of misfits that the general audience wasn't very familiar with. Gunn tried to extend that to the DCU to mixed results. Many have been wondering where Gunn's Batman is, particularly after he was a no-show in Clayface. Gunn did open this universe with Superman, and a sequel is on the way, but it's not quite enough for fans.

The early slate of projects has led to frustrations among viewers that Gunn isn't building enough momentum to bring the biggest characters to the center of the DCU. Ironically, Gunn had recently stated that Superman, Wonder Woman, and Batman were going to be pivotal to the DCU , so it seems he was building to it, but seemingly not fast enough for Skydance.

The Wrap also noted that Latcham will refrain from having a big social media presence, as Gunn was known for being active to a fault. Although he would answer fan questions, he would also sometimes create confusion, get into feuds with fans, and it didn't always create the best image of DC. It's unclear what the next era of DC will look like, but hopefully it's not as chaotic and tumultuous as fans are expecting, since this franchise has been through enough already.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Creature of Darkness - Bottom of the Well Dungeon Walkthrough - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains
articles.body:
Welcome to IGN's Guide to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. After 28 years, Ocarina of Time has been fully remade, and while much of it remains the same, there's plenty of new differences to be found while exploring Hyrule. With the Zora people saved and the Water Medallion secured, Link will have to face a new threat emerging from the depths below Kakariko Village.

Though the ominous Shadow Temple is Link's next objective, getting in won't be possible with Link's current tools, and will require a trip to the Bottom of the Well below the village to find special Lenses of Truth to find the way that has been hidden from view.

After completing the Water Temple, looking back into Hyrule Field will reveal an ominous sight: smoke and fire rising in the direction of Kakariko Village!

Race over across the field on Epona and enter the village. You'll find Sheik alone, standing before the town's well. Before you can act, a creature born of darkness will emerge, knocking Link out and escaping into the nearby Shadow Temple.

When Link awakens, Sheik will tell of how the creature that Impa had sealed away beneath the well long ago had broken, and how Impa left to investigate the Shadow Temple herself, leaving Sheik behind to protect the village. To reach the temple and aid Impa, you'll be given a new melody to learn:

Repeat the prompt to learn the somber Nocturne of Shadow, which can teleport you to an otherwise inaccessible part of the Graveyard behind Kakariko Village. You'll also be given a warning: the temple has many traps to repel intruders that can only be seen with the Eyes of Truth, but Sheik has no idea where to find such a device.

Sure enough, if you try to enter the Shadow Temple yourself, you'll be met with a sealed door and a strange plaque in front of an otherwise empty room.

Instead, be sure to speak with the townsfolk of Kakariko Village after the danger has passed. The old man in particular has an interesting story about a person who lived in the village who had "eyes of truth". Their house stood where the well does today.

If you try to hop down, you'll find a sealed door at the bottom of the well, but there's a small crawlspace too tiny for Link to fit in as an adult, so it's time to take a trip to the past.

Before you do, there's a neat little hidden treasure you can pick up. Latch onto a bit of vines on the low rooftop of Granny's Potion Shop, and look up at the windmill. There's a high opening with a ladder leading to a broken walkway, and you can actually use the Longshot to zip over to the ladder directly.

You can climb up to the top of the Windmill building this way, where you can find a Treasure Chest with a Purple Rupee!

Warp back to the Temple of Time, and return the Master Sword to become a kid again. As a child, the well is still full of water, but if you remember the words from the Music Man in the Windmill when you learned the Song of Storms as an adult, one day a kid appeared and played that song, causing the windmill to spin out of control and drain all the well's water.

It's time to make that paradox a reality. Enter the Windmill and play the Song of Storms for the Music Man, becoming a self-fulfilling prophecy. The well water will drain, allowing you to enter a mini-dungeon much like the Ice Cavern, but even more dangerous given you're still a child.

You'll find this little dungeon to be a lot more open-ended than the Ice Cavern. In fact, there's nothing stopping you from grabbing the most important item in here and then waltzing out without exploring the rest of the place, but since we love to be thorough, we'll touch upon every optional chest and collectible you can find in here. That said, due to the danger of invisible traps, we still highly recommend getting the Lenses of Truth first, and then exploring the rest of this area.

When you first enter the Bottom of the Well, you'll head through a few narrow corridors guarded by Skulltulas. This leads to blank wall with a plaque reading "A wall is not merely a wall. Do not accept only what you see as truth." This will be a recurring theme of this place, and applies to floors as well as walls, so be careful!

Take a leap of faith and move straight into the wall to find its only an illusion. This takes you to a large chamber that makes up the bulk of this mini-dungeon: four long corridors in a square that wrap around a large enclosed room, with a few hallways off to the sides and a larger main corridor leading north.

A large and imposing Green Bubble haunts the four corridors flying in counter-clockwise path. He's impervious to damage while the green flames spread around him, but those flames dissipate whenever he rounds a corner, and in the moments it takes for the Green Bubble to pick up speed again, you can run up from behind and get some hits in. Ambush the monster a few times and you'll be able to take him out permanently, making exploration a bit easier.

Most of the corridors are filled with water, and you can try swimming up, or you can cross the moat to the large central room and find another invisible entrance here, but we recommend avoiding it for the moment. This is because it's full of hidden pitfalls (and a Wallmaster), and there's also a few hiding along the corridors, more notably up in the northeast corner.

There's a large chance that one way or another, you're likely to fall in this pit leading down to B2 early, and it takes a little effort to get back out. Each of the multiple pitfalls all lead back to a large waterlogged area that is full of ReDeads! Even worse, you can't get out through the main exit without finding five Silver Rupees that have been stashed all over the basement.

You'll likely need to start by using the Sun's Song to immobilize and defeat the the two ReDeads down here, as you won't want to be dealing with them every time you fall.

The first two silver Rupees can be found across a series of narrow plants floating in greeze ooze that will damage you if you step in it, so move carefully.

The next two silver Rupees are found close by, one in a pool of water to the northwest, and a second on a dry path in front of some boulders to the north.

Each of the "tendrils" of the basement layout lead to boulders and a pool of water you can fall into from above, but there are several pots full of items by each pool, giving you plenty of bombs to blow your way out.

To find the final silver Rupee, bomb the boulders in the southeastern corner past the green pit. There's more green ooze beyond by the last silver Rupee, which is guarded by one more ReDead sitting in front of a Treasure Chest holding the Dungeon Map!

Now that you have both a map and a way out, head through the unlocked gate to the south to find a ladder you can climb up to a room on the western side of the dungeon.

As it leads back into the main corridors, head to the northern side, where you'll find a series of fountainheads feeding the waterways of this dungeon. In front of the largest fountainhead is the symbol of the Triforce, denoting the Royal Family's seal. Play Zelda's Lullaby here, and the fountains will all cease, lowering the water around the main corridors, and opening up a new area to the north.

Crawl through the tunnel, and defeat the Skulltula in the corridor beyond to enter a room with a small chest at the end. Before you can reach it, you'll fall into a pit leading to a different part of the basement where the boss of this mini-dungeon lies in wait.

Aptly named Dead Hand, the fight will begin with a long and gross looking hand emerging from the ground. The second it can lunge forward and grab you, the true monster will emerge to claim its prey.

The full Dead Hand monster is terrifying to behold, but steel your courage. It will angle its long neck upward as it approaches, and only lower when its ready to take a bite out of its supposed victim. This is your moment to thrash out of the hand's grasp, and then attack Dead Hand full in the face, as it won't take damage anywhere else!

Dead Hand will continue to chase you, lowering its head and giving you a moment to slash at it, but you should soon jump away to the side to avoid its bite and repeat the process. After taking a bit of damage, Dead Hand will turn its back to you and scurry away before burrowing into the ground.

At this point, more and more hands will begin appearing out of the ground all over the arena. This means more chances to get grabbed at all angles, but also more ways to lure Dead Hand from his hiding spot. The only bad news is that struggling in the hand's grasp will slowly eat away at your life.

Keep luring Dead Hand out from his burrowing and waiting until he lowers his grotesque head to slash it or light it up with Din's Fire, and the monstrosity will soon fall. In his place, he'll leave behind this dungeon's treasure: The Lenses of Truth!

With this Sheikah technology, you'll be able to equip it like a mask to the D-Pad Up, and see the unseen. Illusory walls will fade away, invisible pits will reveal themselves, and even special enemies or treasure chests not normally visible can be found! However, using them will slowly use up your Magic Meter, so try not to have them running at all times.

Try it out by looking to the south edge of the pit, and you'll find a hidden ladder you can take back up to the floor above. This corridor has several more hidden alcoves that the Lenses will reveal, and you can help yourself to the pots within. This path exits out onto a hidden ledge above the corridor you entered earlier.

If you look around on top of the mesh platform using the Lenses of Truth, you can find a small Treasure Chest here with a Purple Rupee!

Be sure to also return to the small Treasure Chest that lured you into Dead Hand's lair -- you can now jump over the pit using the Lenses, and help yourself to a Business Scrub Seed.

To help uncover the rest of the hidden treasure of this place, return back to the area with the four corridors past the fountainheads, and use the Lenses of Truth to find a new opening into the large central enclosed room.

Keep your Lenses on, and you'll find many pits here, including around the torture rack in the center, and in the two cells around the south side, with a giant gap blocking access to the large Treasure Chest. Grab the other small Treasure Chest holding a Blue Rupee (guarded by a Skulltula), and then look behind the larger chest to the west.

There's an opening behind it you can only see with the Lenses on, so head back out into the western corridor, and jump through from the mesh platforms to reach the Compass!

There's plenty more goodies to uncover, and a few Gold Skulltulas as well, so let's knock them out one by one.

In the bottom southwest corner of the corridors, there's a hidden ledge leading into a small path to a Deku Business Scrub. He helpfully sells Green Potions (once you beat him up), which can help for prolonged use of the Lenses.

Off to the top northwest, there's another small alcove guarded by Skulltula. Defeat it and use the Lenses to avoid the pits here leading to a small Treasure Chest holding a Red Rupee.

Make your way over to the northeast corner on the opposite side, using the Lenses around a plaque to avoid falling in pits by the door to the east.

In here, there are several Fire Keese you need to be way of along with a Beamos, and a small Treasure Chest in the corner holds some Bombs, but there are many pits in this room you'll need to avoid.

Defeat the group and head into the room to the south. You'll be faced with a Like Like in this brightly-lit room -- be sure to keep your distance and use your Boomerang first to stun it so you can get close enough to attack before retreating again.

Once you've defeated the Like Like in the eastern room of the dungeon, look up on the wall between two torches, and you'll find the first of a few Gold Skulltulas hidden here.

By now you've noticed there are two locked rooms in the northern part of the main central enclosed room with the cells. Finding both keys is next up, and you can leave the room with the Like Like by find a ladder leading back into the eastern corridor.

As you drop down, look into the now dried up waterways below the grating to find a small Treasure Chest holding a Blue Rupee.

While down in the lower part of the waterways, head along the southern corridor, and look for a small drain opening along the bottom of the southwest side. You can crawl through here to find another small Treasure Chest with another Blue Rupee.

Exit out and climb back onto the higher platforms circling the corridors, and head to the east side of the southern corridor while looking north with your Lenses. To the left of the entrance to the central room, there's a small opening in the wall you can leap across to find a small Treasure Chest with a Red Rupee.

There's another identical hiding spot if you head to the southeast corner of the corridors, and use the Lenses here to look toward the central room. Look for the opening to jump through, and this small Treasure Chest hold the first of two Small Keys.

Now with one key in hand, jump back into the central room, and open the locked door in the northeast corner. There's a pit-like room here with few Keese darting about, but you can use your Lenses of Truth to reveal a path around the outer edge, leading to one more Gold Skulltula!

For the other small key, you'll need to head to the only other unexplored area on the west side of the dungeon (Look for a hole from the central room that you can jump across the drained corridor). Where there was once a large flooded pit under a large gate, you'll find that enough water has been drained to dive down and swim to the other side and climb up the mesh walls.

In this last room, you'll find it full of coffins covered in webbing, with several lit torches all around. Each coffin holds something... not all of them good, and you can use a Deku Stick (or Din's Fire) to set the cobwebs ablaze, and find Keese and pots in many, as well a Gibdos. These mummies are like stronger ReDeads, and are fairly resilient, though you can burn them bad with Din's Fire.

Be wary, as the coffins on the north side of the room are hiding another Gibdo, but you can also find Fairy Thoughts in the other coffin, which asks for you to play the song about "going around" Play the Song of Storms, and you can get healed by Fairy Power!

Finally, burn away the lone coffin on the eastern side to find the last remaining Small Key.

Now with the final key, return back across to the central room, this time opening the final locked door in the northwest corner. This small mausoleum room is guarded by a Deku Baba, and in the corner you'll find the last Gold Skulltula to defeat.

You're officially done with the creepy Bottom of the Well, which means it's time to pick up where you left off as an adult.

Before you take back the Master Sword, there's one big thing you can abuse with the Lenses of Truth to get a nice reward. The Treasure Chest Minigame house in Hyrule Castle Town is only open at night, and for 10 Rupees you can try to pick between two chests - one has a small rupee reward, the other a key to move deeper into the rooms for better prizes.

While you can technically win by luck, you now have a pretty definitive edge to win the grand prize easily: Simply wear the Lenses of Truth in each room, and you can see the contents of the chest before you open it. Pick the Small Key every time, and you can make it all the way to the end to earn a Piece of Heart!

When you're ready to proceed, take up the Master Sword to take the Lenses of Truth with you into the future, and warp back to Kakariko Village's Graveyard to enter the dreaded Shadow Temple .

articles.title: Nintendo Opens New Job Role to Preserve and Organize its Old Games
articles.summary: Nintendo of America has opened up a new job position to help preserve and archive the older games in its vast library of titles.
articles.body:
Nintendo of America has opened up a new job position to help preserve and archive the older games in its vast library.

Nintendo has released around 11,000 games in its lifetime. Now, it’s looking to organize those games — at least, the older ones — with a specialized role at its Redmond, WA location.

As per the official job description , Nintendo of America’s future Digital Archivist, Historical Systems will support the “preservation, organization, and accessibility of historical hardware and software information” by designing and implementing a “structured framework for organizing technical records, engineering documentation, source materials, and institutional knowledge related to legacy systems and platforms.”

Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 Gifting Feature Screenshots

Essentially, the digital archivist is a librarian of sorts, whose job is to create a means of organizing and documenting all of Nintendo’s older games, systems, and platforms, as well as any documentation or materials related to them. It definitely sounds like a fun role for video game history buffs, especially if they like organizing data.

The job listing describes its ideal candidate as someone with “expertise in archives, metadata management, information architecture, and research” who will work “closely with subject matter experts across engineering, product development, legal, and business teams” to “establish standards and processes that ensure historical information remains discoverable, usable, and preserved for future generations.”

The position is a 12-month contract role with a salary of $35-$55 per hour. A Bachelor’s degree in library & information science, Archives, Museum Studies, Information Management, History, Technical Communication, or a related field is preferred, although equivalent professional experience may be considered.

This is a major step forward for video game preservation, something that activists and enthusiasts in the space have been calling for for some time now. For example, the Video Game History Foundation was founded in 2016 with the intent of preserving and teaching the history of video games. Since then, it has worked toward creating the United States’ first dedicated library for the study of video game history, as well as preserving games’ source code.

Given Nintendo’s relevance in the games industry and its role in the history of the medium, it makes sense that the company would seek to archive its works. Perhaps this could result in some unexpected discoveries; for example, one collector came across 97 copies of an unreleased version of Super Mario Bros. Duck Hunt earlier this year, five of which were graded perfect 10s by PSA.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is filled with little pieces of dialogue tucked away in secret moments. You can trigger them by talking to a character at a very specific point in time, getting an item out of order and seeing how characters react, and various other ways. There are dozens of interactions that are really easy to miss: I’m on my third playthrough of the remake and am still stumbling into lines of dialogue I didn’t see the first two times around. During a launch event at Nintendo’s New York retail store, I spoke with Nate Bihldorff, Senior Vice President of Product Development and Publishing at Nintendo of America, and asked about how the localization team approaches these small moments.

“My group handles the localization of these games," Bihldorff said. "And I can tell you that the localization team, absolutely, puts the most importance on those single lines that are really, really hard to find. And you know, of course, they are murder on testing teams because finding that specific line and making sure that it appears correctly in the game is super important… But there was always something special about localizing those lines and knowing that only a few people were going to read it, that it took a specific course of action to get there, whether it's in a Zelda game like this or you’re sequence breaking in a Metroid game.

"Knowing that the person who's experiencing that line did something special to get it and wanting to make sure that it had that little extra oomph, I guarantee you the localization team would love to hear you say exactly that… You feel like you're connecting with the developers in those moments. It's a direct line where they're kind of winking at you.”

With so many secrets that exist just for the joy of being secrets, I can’t help but wonder if there are things in Ocarina of Time that no one has found yet. While Bihldorff is quick to point out that he can’t speak on behalf of the developers, he personally likes to think there’s still something hiding in Ocarina of Time that’s a secret to everybody.

“I like to believe that there are. Of course, that's a question for the developers. They probably would be very cagey in the way that they answered it. But I also feel like Nintendo games in general have a wondrous way of having something that you just don't discover forever.”

Part of the reason Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma wanted to develop a remake of Ocarina of Time was so younger developers at Nintendo could familiarize themselves with one of the company’s most influential games. Developers with different levels of experience with the original Ocarina of Time came together to create its Switch 2 remake. Across the Pacific Ocean, the localization team at Nintendo of America had a similar experience.

“As someone who was also around for the original, I feel like it was almost doubly meaningful because you really feel the opportunity to not only be a part of something that was so meaningful for a previous generation of fans, but also be there at the moment that a new generation who had never played it before are going to experience it in really this unbelievably beautiful and well thought-out state.”

Internally at Nintendo of America, Bihldorff said that mix of generations led to different perspectives during localization: “You get to talk to somebody who maybe worked on the original game, and the IP has a specific meaning for [them], and then, a younger staff who's maybe coming in right out of school in their early 20s who, of course they've heard of it, but I'm seeing them experiencing these things for the first time… That sort of estuary water mix I think is something that's really, really important for the creative process, and it keeps this company vibrant. It's certainly something that I feed off of.”

The sense of anticipation was obvious as Nintendo employees prepared for the midnight launch while fans lined up outside. Nintendo of America is a very secretive place, and I’m always curious to learn what the process is like when they first get word of what the developers in Japan are working on years before a public event like this.

“I think it's not me pulling the curtain too far back to be able to say that every single one of these games is met with tremendous enthusiasm the second we hear about them. It’s a tough job sometimes, being behind the scenes when you can't talk to anybody. We don't talk to our spouses and stuff like that about it. It's a lot of secret stuff. And yet we're also passionate about the work and, of course, making sure that we bring the developers’ visions to market in a way that makes it proud. Everybody takes it very seriously, but they're also huge fans. So yeah, I can say, absolute excitement when we heard about this.”

After years of working in secrecy, Nintendo now hands Ocarina of Time off to the fans. One such fan at the launch event was Grammy, Oscar, and Emmy-winning musician Jon Batiste, who spoke to me about how The Legend of Zelda’s music influenced him from a young age, starting with Link’s Awakening on the Game Boy.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Launch Photos

“When I was a kid and my sister, who was really my hero, she had a Game Boy and we would play. Every day, we rode up and down the street and she would play first, and then when the battery was almost out, she would give it to me and I would play until the battery ran completely out," Batiste said. "And I realized at that point, okay, I'm pretty much going to be doing this for the rest of my life.

“And then when I started to play Nintendo 64, that's when I started with Ocarina of Time and the music captured me. And I started to actually play those scores on instruments. And I played tons of scores from Nintendo games on the piano. My cousin and I actually, we have a video of us as a band when we first started playing, and our repertoire was probably 50% Nintendo franchise themes. So then we started to research who were the composers of the scores and we started to really pick favorites, like Koji Kondo. The sound of those melodies, I would say, was an early compositional influence.”

For more on The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, check out my interview with producers Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi . And, read about the launch event on the other coast, where Ryan McCaffrey spoke to Nintendo of America’s Bill Trinen .

Logan Plant is IGN's Senior Editor, Playlist and DB, and the host of Nintendo Voice Chat. The Legend of Zelda is his favorite video game franchise of all time, and he is patiently awaiting the day Nintendo announces a brand new F-Zero. articles.title: I Tried the Pokémon Happy Meal — Here’s What I Learned (and What I Pulled)
articles.body:
Pokémon Happy Meals have officially returned, and if the swarm of teenagers in my generally quiet local McDonald’s is anything to go by, they’re bigger than ever.

The Pokémon Company first announced the return of its McDonald's promotion several weeks back, causing some confusion by accidentally spoiling next year’s promo card list . Good times.

Now that I’ve gotten my hands on the 30th Anniversary Happy Meal, I can confirm the previously leaked card set is in fact the accurate one, along with new details about the promotion’s roll-out.

30th Anniversary Pokémon Happy Meal - Images

The Pokémon Happy Meal is available in all of McDonald’s traditional Happy Meal variants: hamburger, cheeseburger, or 4 and 6-piece nugget combos. Prices vary based on your meal selection, but every option comes with the same packaging and blind-boxed toys.

I was surprised to find how little my local McDonald’s was seemingly marketing the collab, which presumably varies across locations. My McDonald’s only had one poster, and otherwise sporadically flashed the Pokémon Happy Meal teaser on its digital ordering screens.

For reference, when I went to Target’s Pokémon launch , the whole store was covered in Pokémon materials. Many of these posters and stands ended up on eBay , so it’s possible TPC is now limiting its 'physical' marketing footprint to help stores avoid any tussles or, you know, crime.

While some social media users are claiming their local McDonald’s is approaching the collab as a progressive roll-out, my local D.C. McDonald’s had all three boxes and 15 promo cards ready to go. A staff member, however, did acknowledge that other stores may be receiving the promotional materials "in batches."

Given the swarms of kids and teenagers who had seemingly abandoned school for Pokémon, I was only willing to pick up two Happy Meals. (A six-nugget and a cheeseburger, in case you were curious.) The working manager was kind enough to ensure I got two different Pokémon boxes, which ended up being Torchic and Pikachu.

I quickly realized that was a strategic choice — almost every other customer was specifically requesting (and getting) the Umbreon box, so the staff was trying to manage its stock.

Of course, one of the main draws of the collaboration is new promo cards, which often end up reselling at the same price as the Happy Meal itself. While rumors had already been circulating online, I was still shocked to discover they really do give you the two promo cards without any packaging. They’re slipped into a box right next to a hard plastic toy that, for whatever reason, does get delicate tissue paper wrapping. The box, at least, is definitely serviceable for storing decks.

I’ll admit the lack of packaging does make the card reveal less climactic, and I can imagine there’s already someone complaining out there about getting a damaged card. Still, I don’t mind Pokemon treating its promo cards a little more casually in the interest of promoting the TCG as a game to be played as opposed to a collector’s racket.

I anti-climactically slid out Eevee and Tyranitaur from my first box, then found Zoroark and Chandelure in my second one. Each card is a reprint marked with the M26 label and its own numbering system, and some have holo foil. You can see the (real) full list of 2026 promo cards here .

The other toy you get is a miniature plastic version of the Happy Meal box themed after an individual Pokémon, with the full slate shown below. Each toy box has a clip you can use to attach it to a bag or keychain, and I happened to get Diglit and good ol' Pikachu.

This is far from Pokémon’s first time teaming up with the fast-food giant. The partnership goes all the way back to 1999, when Pokémania first hit its stride. The modern 'Pokémon Happy Meal' first launched in 2011.

It was only natural that the promotion would return for the year of Pokémon’s 30th anniversary, offering what I believe to be one of the best budget-friendly ways for fans to get involved in the festivities. Safe to say, I'm satisfied, albeit still hungry.

The Pokémon Happy Meal is now available across all U.S. McDonald’s locations through December 14. The promotion will be expanding to additional countries over the next couple of months, with the full roll-out detailed in an official McDonald’s post .

Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

articles.title: Shaquille O'Neal is Starring in a Game Show Where Players Have to Hide Him in Plain Sight
articles.summary: In one of the more amusing sidequests that Shaquille O’Neal has undertaken in his life, the former NBA All-Star is set to appear in a game show where players try to conceal him from view in a hilarious twist on hide-and-seek.
articles.body:
In one of the more amusing sidequests that Shaquille O’Neal has embarked on in his life, the former NBA All-Star is set to appear in a game show where players try to conceal him from view in a hilarious twist on hide-and-seek.

Can You Hide… Shaq? Is the name of this upcoming game show, which will premiere with two episodes at 9 PM on Thursday, December 3, on ABC and the ESPN app. Episodes will be available to stream on Hulu starting December 4.

The show pits two teams of contestants against each other, challenging them to hide Shaq in plain sight in public areas around Dallas, Texas. This is no small feat, given that Shaq is a massive former athlete and one of the world's most recognizable celebrities.

“I’m 7-foot-1. I’m not exactly easy to miss,” Shaquille O’Neal said, per Variety . “I love meeting people wherever I go, but for years I’ve always wondered, could somebody actually make me disappear? Well, we finally decided to put it to the test. We turned it into a real competition, and I can’t wait for you to see the creative, ridiculous ways they tried to hide me in plain sight. The stakes are high, and so is the prize. But you know me, we’re gonna have some fun along the way.”

Comedian Nicole Byer will host the program, which promises to be a competition full of “fast, funny, and unpredictable challenges.”

The show's logline lays out the rules: “Contestants first split into two teams, each with a set mission and time clock. The team that completes its mission with the fewest spottings earns immunity for one team member in the next round, who then becomes team captain. The teams must work together toward one greater mission: earning prize money to add to the ‘Shaq-pot’ that will ultimately be claimed by one winner.”

As of yet, the amount in the ‘Shaq-pot’ is unknown, but it had better be worth it, given how undoubtedly difficult it is to disguise one of the NBA’s most famous players. Can you hide… Shaq? Is produced by Jersey Legends Productions and Fulwell Entertainment in partnership with ESPN. Executive producers listed are Shaquille O’Neal, Colin Smeeton, Jeremy Castro, Charlie Van Vleet, Adam Cooper, Ben Winston, Mike Paris, and Emma Conway.

Shaq has undertaken no small amount of passion projects in his career; aside from his legacy as a sports legend, he's also a dubstep artist (under the name DJ Diesel), rapper, actor, and has even appeared in a few video games, including Fortnite and of course, Shaq Fu .

I personally can't wait to see how contestants manage to hide Shaq in this show. Let us know what your strategy would be in the comments, and whether or not you'll be watching come December 3.

articles.title: Where to Get Bugs - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Bugs are small gold and blue insects found under rocks and in tall grass in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. They are not enemies, but rather a
articles.body:
Bugs are small gold and blue insects found under rocks and in tall grass in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. They are not enemies, but rather a resource you can capture in an Empty Bottle. Releasing a Bug near Magic Bean Soil causes the Bug to go inside, revealing a Gold Skulltula.

If you are in a grassy or forested area, you can sometimes find a Bug by simply cutting down all the nearby grass and plants. Bugs have a small chance to appear, just like a Rupee or Heart.

If you would rather get your Bugs in bulk, the best spot is the small plot of farmland just outside Kakariko Village. There is a grotto here surrounded by plants, and cutting them produces about a half a dozen Bugs at once.

You can also visit the grotto in the Lost Woods (found next to the shortcut to Goron City), though this requires Bombs to gain entry.

Finally, you can also purchase a Bug at various stores across the game for 30 Rupees. We would recommend forgoing this option as they are so abundant elsewhere!

articles.title: Serpico Questline Guide - Probably Stolen Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Serpico is a young cadet whom you meet while playing Probably Stolen. He's recently joined the Security force as someone who wants to destroy the
articles.body:
Serpico is a young cadet whom you meet while playing Probably Stolen . He's recently joined the Security force as someone who wants to destroy the corruption within it. However, he soon realizes that he's in over his head, and you have the opportunity to help out during your time as a shop merchant. In this guide, we're going to cover everything you need to know about how to complete Serpico's Questline while playing Probably Stolen.

How to Complete Serpico's Questline in Probably Stolen

Serpico has a chance to appear around the first month after you begin your initial start as a shopkeeper. There have been times when he shows up earlier, even before Eleanor does, but expect him before you purchase the Business Permit. Serpico introduces himself as a brand new cadet, and it's his first day on the job. He's proud of his work, even though his family views him as a traitor. On his first day, he's going to ask if you have any snacks for sale to share with his colleagues.

Serpico appears a few days after this initial meeting. He comes to you telling you that working in Security is not what he expected, and the corruption is even worse than he thought. It's everywhere, and he has no idea how to help with it. He requests a drink from you and asks if you'll sell him any alcoholic beverages before departing. It's not a requirement to sell him any.

The next time you see Serpico, he's going to tell you he went to his higher-ups about the corruption. He's excited to hear that they were happy to hear about these reports, and he's looking forward to an upcoming promotion. To celebrate, he wants to buy more food from you, and swears off drinking alcohol while he's working. You can sell food to him before he departs.

Shortly after this previous event, another Security officer appears asking if you've seen Serpico. They inform you that Serpico is wanted for corruption charges, as he was caught recently drinking on the job. She wants you to call Security the next time you see him, and they'll give you 300 Credits. Serpico appears a day after this event, explaining that they are trying to pin everything on him. He disappears after this encounter, not asking to buy anything, only saying that he's going to be hiding at the Dumping Grounds.

After Serpico disappears, Georgio will appear with a handwritten note from Serpico. He explains that he got shot while attempting to escape the Security and needs food sent to him. He needs at least 2,000 kcal of food sent to him. You can do this by making your way to the Dumping Grounds at night and dropping it off on the ground for Serpico to pick up. This could take a handful of trips for you to complete. There's also the chance that Georgio will offer to do this for you if you'd rather he went there, and you didn't waste your time at night. Between the two, I recommend doing it yourself.

Following this event, another Security officer will approach you. They share that they're raising the bounty on Serpico and will provide 600 Credits if you apprehend him. You'll have a chance to do this when Serpico approaches you in disguise within a few days. Here, he shares that he's gathered up the last of the evidence he's needed to reveal the corruption in Security. As he decides what to do with it, he asks you for advice on what he should do.

You have three choices: Sell it to the black market, give it to the Revolution , or provide these details to trusted members of the Security force . If you want to suggest that Serpico give it to the Security force, you need at least 50 Faction with them to make it happen. Of these three options, selling it to the Black Market is the worst. If you make this choice, Serpico later turns out dead, and the Black Market gives you credits for handing him over.

If you go with the Revolution or the Security force, they provide similar rewards. Serpico later joins the Revolution in a fight against the Security if you tell him to go to the Revolution. But if you tell him to go to the higher-ranking officers, he returns as the head of the anti-corruption force for Security. Both of these choices keep Serpico alive, and he provides you with one of three rewards: a Storage Bay with extended space, four Module Bay Expansion Kits, or two Current Converters. You can choose from these three rewards.

articles.title: Lanterns Not Renewed for Season 2, Says DC Studios Insider
articles.summary: An insider at DC Studios claims that HBO’s Lanterns was not renewed for a second season in spite of rave reviews and audience interest, as told in a report from Variety.
articles.body:
An insider at DC Studios claims that HBO’s Lanterns was not renewed for a second season in spite of rave reviews and audience interest, as told in a report from Variety.

Variety’s report comes on the heels of James Gunn and Peter Safran’s exit from DC Studios on Monday, November 9. In a statement to the public, Gunn cited a dislike for the more “corporate” aspect of his position, citing long hours that negatively impacted his personal relationships.

Unsurprisingly, fans are now worried about the future of the DCU, given that Gunn had only been in his role for four years with just three films to show for it. Superman was released to generally positive reception; Supergirl decidedly less so; Clayface was also a mixed bag, but Lanterns , the live-action show that released on HBO this year, was a massive success .

Boasting viewership numbers that rivaled the likes of The Pitt , it’s safe to say that audiences loved Kyle Chandler’s Hal Jordan and Aaron Pierre’s John Stewart, and hopes were high for a second season. In fact, it seemed almost inevitable — but, according to insiders, it didn’t quite “capture the zeitgeist.” Whatever that means.

Variety’s report says this insider pointed out that the series “didn’t get renewed for a second season,” telling the outlet, “People cannot wait to make another season of a hit show.”

This news, if true, comes as quite a shock — but that seems to be the theme of the month, given Safran and Gunn’s unexpected exit. In October, series co-creator Damon Lindelof revealed that writers were already hashing out ideas for a second season , though it hadn’t been greenlit just yet.

Safran confirmed this news in an October interview with IGN , though he admitted that it hinged on whether or not the team could come up with a story worth following up from the first season.

"The episodic world is always going to be a really important part of our overall slate, it's a great way to tell stories that need more real estate than a feature film can offer you, and it's a great way to introduce characters that we then bring into the feature world," Safran told us. "And I think that Aaron Pierre and John Stewart are a perfect example of that. We introduced him in Lanterns, and audiences will see him next summer in Man of Tomorrow. So, it's really important to us in continuing to tell aspects of the story that we're not telling in the feature film world, so there's more to come.

"Listen, we'll see what happens with Lanterns Season 2. If, I think, the collective group of HBO and DC and Chris Mundy and the team all feel like we've got something that is a worthy successor to quite a beloved first season of television, then I wouldn't be surprised to see more."

While official news on the future of Lanterns remains up in the air, this report paints a grim picture for the future of the DCU which was, somewhat tragically, only just getting started.

articles.summary: The Treasure Chest Shop is a mini-game in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. This mini-game can be found in the back alleys of Castle Town, though it
articles.body:
The Treasure Chest Shop is a mini-game in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. This mini-game can be found in the back alleys of Castle Town, though it is only open at night time. This page will explain how to win the Treasure-Chest Shop game, and its rewards.

Check out IGN's full guide to the Treasure-Chest Shop mini-game below.

Locate the Treasure-Chest Shop in the back alley of Castle Town, it is the building with the treasure chest sign on the west side of town.

Head inside and speak to the Treasure-Chest Shopkeeper, who will let you test your "luck" for 10 Rupees per play.

The concept of the game is this: in each room are two chests. One has a Rupee, the other a Small Key. Choose the Small Key and you get to advance, choose the Rupee and you lose, but get to keep the winnings. To get the grand prize you need to guess right five times in a row, which is unlikely.

Thankfully there is a solution. Wearing the Lenses of Truth (found in the Bottom of the Well dungeon in Kakariko Village) lets you see the contents of the chests, guaranteeing you get the key each time. Use them to easily make your way to the final room and claim your prize: a Piece of Heart.

articles.title: Microsoft’s DLSS competitor is out for the Xbox Ally X and works in handheld mode
articles.summary: Microsoft is now rolling out Auto SR for the Xbox Ally X, Xbox Ally X20, and select Windows Copilot Plus PCs, and also adding Auto SR for handheld mode.
articles.body: Microsoft is now rolling out Automatic Super Resolution (Auto SR), an upscaling technology that competes with Nvidia’s DLSS, for the Xbox Ally X, Xbox Ally X20, and select Windows Copilot Plus PCs, the company announced today. Auto SR is also getting some new features alongside this official release. In April, Microsoft started testing Auto SR on the Xbox Ally X, but you could only use it while docked. The full release of Auto SR announced today now works while you’re playing handheld and running on battery, and it also supports games running at 1080p. Microsoft does note that playing in handheld and at 1080p might lead to performance that “may not be as optimal as other configurations,” but says you’ll see visual improvements “especially in older games.” Previously, Auto SR was also limited to framerates of “around” 60 to 75fps, but support for a new Auto SR Performance mode will allow you to hit framerates of up to 120fps. The Performance mode, and new compatibility with Auto HDR, will be available through Windows updates.

articles.title: How to Get the Golden Gauntlets - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Golden Gauntlets are the final upgrade to Link's lifting strength in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. These gauntlets allow Link to lift
articles.body:
The Golden Gauntlets are the final upgrade to Link's lifting strength in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. These gauntlets allow Link to lift even the heaviest blocks and pillars. This page will explain how to get the Golden Gauntlets, and what other items you can obtain with their power.

Check out IGN's complete guide to the Golden Gauntlets below.

The Golden Gauntlets are the final dungeon item in the entire game, found in Ganondorf's Castle. They allow you to lift the gold and black Ganon pillars, an upgrade from the Silver Gauntlets which only let you lift the black Ganon pillars.

To reach Ganondorf's Castle, you must complete every single Temple then speak to Zelda at the Temple of Time. Once you are inside the castle, head straight for the Shadow Trial (the door marked with the Shadow Medallion symbol).

Inside the Shadow Trial is a massive room sparsely filled with platforms. To cross, you need to first light the torch in the distance with a Fire Arrow (or, shoot a regular arrow through the torch by the door toward the torch in the distance). This will cause a set of platforms to appear, allowing you to cross to the platform on the other side.

Here you first need to defeat the Like Like (you can stun it with your Longshot), then equip the Hover Boots and cross over to the next nearest platform, with the black and gold pillar on it. Look right and you will see a platform with a button on it. Use the Hover Boots again to float over there (or use the Lenses of Truth to see the invisible platforms connecting to it).

Open the chest to receive your shiny new upgrade!

With your fancy new Golden Gauntlets equipped, there is one other upgrade you can quickly get: the Gift of Halved Damage . Exit Ganondorf's Castle, cross the rainbow bridge, then go left toward the dead end. Lift the black and gold pillars to reveal the entrance to a Great Fairy Fountain, where you can pay 500 Rupees for the permanent half damage upgrade!

articles.title: The DCU Regime Change Threatens to Turn Man of Tomorrow Into 2027’s Answer to The Flash
articles.summary: It’s been four years since James Gunn and Peter Safran were announced as the co-bosses of DC Studios, and just a day since their ouster was revealed, and we're having a serious case of déjà vu.
articles.body:
It’s fall 2022 and a new regime is announced as taking over DC’s film and TV future even as a major DC movie from the prior regime continues in post-production for release the following summer.

It’s fall 2026 and a new regime is announced as taking over DC’s film and TV future even as a major DC movie from the prior regime continues in post-production for release the following summer.

It’s been four years since James Gunn and Peter Safran were announced as the co-bosses of DC Studios, and just a day since their ouster was revealed, and this nerd reporter is having a serious case of déjà vu.

When Gunn and Safran took the reins of DC in October 2022, they were inheriting several projects that were already far into production: the headline-plagued The Flash , Blue Beetle , and Batgirl .

In 2023, The Flash marked the end of a DC film continuity created just a handful of years earlier — the DCEU, aka the Snyderverse — that would see a group of DC heroes, including Supergirl, band together to stop a cosmic threat to Earth led by one of Superman’s greatest foes.

In 2027, Man of Tomorrow will potentially mark the end of a DC film continuity created just a handful of years earlier — the DCU — that will see a group of DC heroes, including Supergirl , band together to stop a cosmic threat to Earth led by one of Superman’s greatest foes.

The Flash had its heroes out to stop General Zod, while Man of Tomorrow will feature Brainiac (in his live-action film debut). The parallels between the end of Snyder’s DCEU and Gunn’s DCU are depressingly similar. In both cases, new regimes were taking hold of the reins of Warner Bros. and resetting the priorities of its most important superhero IP with little regard to the projects and characters that fans had been conditioned to believe were going to matter going forward.

The regime change of 2022 told fans that the upcoming DC films no longer mattered because they would be ret-conned out of the next iteration of the DC Universe.

Is that where we’re at now with the DCU? Until newly appointed DC Studios boss Jeremy Latcham says otherwise, fans can only suspect we’re back to square one again with upcoming DC projects (unless they heed some fans’ advice not to reboot the DCU again). If that’s it for Gunn and Safran’s “Gods and Monsters,” then why should fans be invested in Man of Tomorrow if it no longer matters? It will just collapse in on itself as The Flash did.

I was at Warner Bros. in late January 2023 when James Gunn and Peter Safran announced their “Gods and Monsters” roadmap . Even then, the invited press, myself included, couldn’t mask our doubts. Haven’t we seen these big presentations and slate reveals before only for them to never materialize? (I was also at a San Diego Comic-Con panel when DC announced a Cyborg solo film , which obviously never happened.)

At that launch event, Gunn and Safran did their best to persuade us that this time would be different. Sadly, it wasn’t. Whatever plans the new DC Studios regime under Jeremy Latcham announces should be met with a comparable degree of skepticism because it could all be over, once again, in a Flash.

articles.title: Fortis Games Closes With Over 400 Jobs Impacted
articles.summary: Fortis Games, a studio behind mobile titles like Twilight Towers and Bloom & Breakfast, has closed its doors, impacting around 440 jobs.
articles.body:
Fortis Games, a studio behind mobile titles like Twilight Towers and Bloom & Breakfast, has closed its doors, impacting around 440 jobs.

CEO Steven Chiang confirmed the closure in a statement to GamesBeat on November 10, 2026. “Fortis has been a labor of love for so many of us and we’re disappointed we weren’t able to achieve the goals we set for ourselves when we started this journey more than five years ago,” he told the outlet.

“We have been fortunate to work with some of the most talented and dedicated people in this space. As we move forward, our primary focus will be on helping this talented team of individuals find new opportunities. Thank you to everyone who has supported us over the past five years. We are grateful for the collaboration and friendship we have shared with so many.”

Several former employees have spoken out about the closure in posts on LinkedIn. In one of these posts, game producer Gustavo Coronet confirmed that Las Vegas Sands Corp., Fortis Games’ parent company, chose to “end funding and part ways, terminating all of the contracts, worldwide.”

“Super proud of the work we’ve done. LVS’s decision does not delete the ground breaking and best-in class agentic development workflow the Octopus team has built, nor the massively solid soft launch metrics both our projects were achieving in such early stages of development,” he wrote.

In another post, former communications director Scott Butterworth suggested that Fortis’s “community-focused” approach to mobile games didn’t resonate enough with players to help it “get off the ground.”

“Ah, Fortis Games — what could have been. Despite our unique, community-focused approach to the mobile games market, we just couldn't seem to get off the ground, and today, we finally ran out of runway,” he wrote.

“The company has officially shuttered, abruptly putting more than 400 talented people out of work (myself included). Hilariously, I'm also in the process of relocating to Los Angeles, so hey, why not add a little more change on top, right?”

Fortis Gaming was founded in 2022 by Steven Chiang, former executive at Electronic Arts and Zynga. Based out of San Francisco, California, it was funded by Las Vegas Sands Corp. to help the casino brand expand outside of gambling. Fortis went on to acquire several games studios over the ensuing four years; on November 4, it announced that it was sunsetting Twilight Towers , a move that came a mere week before Fortis’s total closure.

This is the latest game studio to shut its doors after EA revealed that it had closed down BioWare , famous for AAA RPG series like Mass Effect and Dragon Age — a decision that has proven to be extremely unpopular among players, who are now campaigning for EA to do something , anything, with its IP to prevent them from languishing in obscurity.

articles.body:
The Forsaken Oath armor is a unique armor set in Crimson Desert introduced with the Charting the Unknown DLC. If you don't have a diving suit, this armor set will help you hold your breath longer so you can explore the depths of Pywel's ocean. This page details the locations of all four pieces of the Forsaken Oath armor set hidden on the seafloor in Crimson Desert.

There are four pieces of the Forsaken Oath set in Crimson Desert.

The Forsaken Oath Plate Helm is hidden in an underwater chest at the Great Hydrothermal Vents between Bergel Island and Nirakan Island in the South Sea. Directly above the "T" in "Great," dive down 200 meters to the seabed.

Look for a trio of bright glowing volcanic rocks surrounding two active hydrothermal vents. The chest is embedded in a stone deposit a few meters south of there. If you see a Manganese deposit, you're in the right place.

The Forsaken Oath Plate Armor is located in a sunken chest just off the northern coast of Ocula Island at the southeastern corner of the map.

At 50 to 60 meters below the surface, there's a huge shipwreck. You'll find the treasure chest embedded in a stone deposit in between the halves of the destroyed ship.

The Forsaken Oath Plate Gloves are found in a sunken treasure chest in the Great Coral Reef northwest of Xamaca Island. To reach it, dive 120 meters down to the seafloor slightly southeast of the "C" in "Coral."

At the bottom, you'll find a big boulder covered in coral and guarded by stone golems that spring to life when you approach. The chest is embedded in a bright yellow ore deposit surrounded by air bubbles rising to the surface.

The Forsaken Oath Plate Boots are located in a sunken treasure chest off the northern coast of Razanui Island in the southwestern corner of the map. It's only about 15 meters below the surface. Dive down to the spot marked on the map below to reach it.

You'll find a bunch of Shiny Ore nodes on a big boulder that's tall enough to slightly poke above sea level. The chest is embedded in a stone deposit across from those nodes to the north.

articles.title: Marvel's VisionQuest Doesn't Entirely Stick the Landing in Its Final Episode, as a New MCU Villain Fails to Make an Impression
articles.summary: The last-minute addition of a new villain derails the finale of VisionQuest somewhat, but the series still succeeds where Vision and Ultron are concerned.
articles.body:
Full spoilers ahead for VisionQuest Episode 8!

VisionQuest has certainly gained momentum with time, to the point where it easily ranks among the best of Marvel's live-action Disney+ shows to date (not that it looks like there's going to be much competition in the foreseeable future ). Sadly, that momentum doesn't entirely carry over into the final episode. "Forever" is a bit of a letdown compared to recent installments of the series, mainly due to the last-minute pivot to a new villain.

James Spader has so often stolen the spotlight as Ultron in this series. But here, Spader proves to be both the best and worst element of the finale. His Ultron remains as compelling and entertaining as ever, but Spader can't quite bring that appeal over to his new role as the shadowy "Client," aka Virgil Horton. There's something about Horton that just doesn't resonate as strongly as Ultron does. It's hard to say if the problem is more the quality of the dialogue or the comparatively manic way Spader is playing him, but Horton comes across as more annoying than threatening. You can't argue the actor isn't giving it his all here (including in that kooky little dance number), but as an endgame villain, Virgil Horton is lacking a certain je ne sais quoi.

Part of it comes down to the notion that Ultron is based on a human model in the first place. The series lightly teased this a few episodes back when Ultron insisted to F.R.I.D.A.Y. that he was unique. Well, it turns out he isn't. It diminishes this villain a bit to see that all his acerbic, affected charm comes not from being invented in a lab by Tony Stark and immediately exposed to the horrors of the Internet, but because he's a copy of Jo Carrington's (T'Nia Miller) creepy ex-boyfriend. Ultimately, I might have been happier if the series had culminated with the more predictable reveal that Phineas Horton (Paul Bettany) or J.I.M. were the Client.

With all that in mind, it's just as well that the finale eventually wipes its hands of Virgil Horton and shifts back to the core rivalry between Vision and Ultron. Horton's death scene is amusing in its abruptness, though it is a little strange having Ultron drop a wisecrack one-liner immediately after seeing his beloved Jocasta gunned down. Regardless, though, the episode makes the most of Ultron's grief at losing the woman he so obsessively loves. It's quite a shift for a character who previously wanted to wipe out humanity for no other reason than pure contempt for his creators. Last time around, the Avengers stopped Ultron by force. This time, Vision does it alone by appealing to Ultron's latent humanity.

The finale also benefits from a steady dose of action, both within and without the Horton mansion. We finally get to see more of Vision and Ultron in their unfiltered android forms, including a rather stylish costume redesign for Vision himself. On that front, at least, this episode doesn't disappoint.

Also satisfying is the way "Forever" focuses on Vision's little family unit. We finally get the big reunion between Tommy (Ruaridh Mollica) and Billy (Joe Locke), as the latter pierces the magical veil to track down his long-lost brother. I fully expected the series to do nothing more than allude to Billy's existence in the end, so actually getting some meaningful interaction between the brothers is a treat. And am I mistaken, or was that a genuinely new (if exceedingly brief) cameo shot of Wanda (Elizabeth Olsen) when Vision is being tortured in the dining room? Either way, the series certainly wants us to walk away with the impression that the entire family will be happily reunited at some point post-Avengers: Secret Wars.

I do think the episode takes the whole "found family" conceit a little too far by having Vision, Tommy, Lisa (Lauren Morais) and all the A.I. units partner up with Paladin (Todd Stashwick) in the end. Obviously, Paladin himself experienced a bit of a redemption arc over time, but are we forgetting the fact that he was responsible for J.A.R.V.I.S.'s death back in Episode 2? Having everyone go full buddy/buddy feels too cute by half.

Ultimately, "Forever" acts as a decent but flawed cap to a generally strong Marvel series. I wish the execution had been stronger on the Virgil Horton front, but at least the series succeeds in terms of wrapping up Vision and Ultron's arcs.

articles.title: Phantom Ship Blueprint Location - Crimson Desert Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Phantom Ship is one of the best ships in Crimson Desert's Charting the Unknown DLC, but it requires a special blueprint before you can unlock it.
articles.body:
The Phantom Ship is one of the best ships in Crimson Desert 's Charting the Unknown DLC, but it requires a special blueprint before you can unlock it. You'll also need a ton of materials from Pywel's ocean in order to craft it afterward. This page shows you exactly where to find the Phantom Ship blueprint in Crimson Desert.

Where to Find the Phantom Ship Blueprint

The Phantom Ship blueprint is found in a buried treasure chest on Illya Island near the southern edge of the map. You'll find it on the southwestern side of the island.

The chest is buried right next to the Rocky Hill Ocean Ruins of Illya Island puzzle with the rotating mural of a whale. Head there (or fast travel to the Abyss Cresset if you've already solved the puzzle), and then look to the north.

Ignore the footpath along the cliff's edge. Instead, drop down to the area below the path with the stone mounds.

You'll find the treasure chest buried next to some stacked cairn stones and red plants. Use a shovel to remove the surrounding dirt and dig it up.

Once you've found and read the Phantom Ship blueprint, you still need to craft the vessel before you can set sail. It's one of the most expensive items in the game, requiring the following materials:

Obsidian can be found on the southern islands of Pywel's ocean, particularly Estra Island, Bergel Island, and Satyros Island. Look out for dark ore nodes among the gray cliffs.

Giant Jellyfish Skin can be harvested from Giant Jellyfish, which spawn rarely in the Great Coral Reef region. You can tell them apart from other jellyfish by their bright pink color (and large size). Hunt for these at night to spot them more easily!

Finally, Natural Pearls are the hardest ingredients to get. They can very rarely be found in clams at the deepest parts of the ocean, but you can also obtain them from a Greymane dispatch mission on Illya Island. Pioneer the island, then repeat the dispatch mission to stock up.
